WhyItMatters: This is the single behaviour the registry exists to guarantee; getting it wrong makes every historical certification unreadable.
FollowUps: Are published versions immutable? / What does the record store to make this work? / What happens for a split competency?
SampleAnswerShape: states version immutability, the record's stored version reference, and the crosswalk path for split or merged competencies

Question: What is the blast radius when the registry is unavailable while an assessment is mid-flight?
WhyItMatters: If assessment fails closed the learner loses a session; if it fails open the record is written against an unresolved competency and is undefendable.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-03.3.01 registry SLO); Architecture Review Report §W answer 14
FollowUps: Is the posture fail-open or fail-closed? / Do consumers cache definitions? / How long may a cached definition be used?
SampleAnswerShape: states the declared posture per consumer and the maximum permitted cache age

Question: If a CaSS-class project is wrapped behind an EdVidura-owned contract, who owns the competency vocabulary when the upstream project changes its model?
WhyItMatters: Wrapping hides an upstream model change until it breaks resolution for records already written, inside enclaves that cannot be patched quickly.
BlocksWork: TLA-02.1.03 sourcing decision and exit strategy
FollowUps: Who watches upstream releases? / Is the wrapper contract version-frozen? / What is the fork trigger?
SampleAnswerShape: names the upstream-watch owner, the contract-freeze rule and the fork or replace trigger

Question: Should EdVidura deploy a CaSS-class registry or build a thin PostgreSQL registry behind its own published contract?
WhyItMatters: Adopting an upstream project buys a standards-aligned model and inherits its governance health; building buys control and costs the competency model from scratch.
AnswerSource: Decision Register DEC-004; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-02.1.01, TLA-02.1.03); Risk R-015
FollowUps: What is the exit strategy under each? / Does either meet the enclave install requirement? / Who audits upstream governance health?
SampleAnswerShape: compares both against schema requirements, enclave packaging and exit strategy, and names the deciding authority

Question: Is a competency count comparable across two frameworks joined only by partial-equivalence crosswalk entries?
WhyItMatters: Presenting partial equivalences as satisfied competencies produces an enterprise readiness number that overstates capability.
FollowUps: How are partials rendered on a dashboard? / Can partials be summed at all? / Who signs off cross-framework reporting?
SampleAnswerShape: states the rendering rule for partial equivalence and whether aggregation across frameworks is permitted

Question: What does language-neutral competency identity mean and why are labels stored separately from definitions?
WhyItMatters: If a competency is identified by its English label, a Hindi assessment asserts a different competency and cross-language readiness comparison silently breaks.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.1.02, TST-32.2.03); Architecture Review Report §V.3
FollowUps: How is a locale label added after publication? / What if no label exists for a locale? / Does the label version with the framework?
SampleAnswerShape: separates the identifier from its localised labels and states what an official record stores

Question: What happens to a crosswalk mapping when one of the two frameworks it maps publishes a new version?
WhyItMatters: A silently surviving crosswalk lets an Indian-framework record be presented as satisfying an enterprise competency that the new version redefined.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-91.1.04 crosswalk decay rule)
FollowUps: Is the mapping invalidated automatically? / Is its use blocked during re-review? / Who re-approves it?
SampleAnswerShape: names the invalidation trigger, the blocked-usage rule and the re-approval route

Question: How does a framework update reach an enclave that syncs quarterly before assessments there run against a stale definition?
WhyItMatters: An enclave assessing against a superseded competency definition issues official records that the enterprise tier cannot interpret consistently.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.2.04); Architecture Review Report §D-M19 gap 6
FollowUps: Is there a per-class staleness bound? / Is assessment blocked past the bound? / Who is notified when the bound is breached?
SampleAnswerShape: names the replica model, the staleness bound and the assessment-blocking rule

Question: How would you detect that two loaded frameworks contain colliding competency identifiers or overlapping definitions?
WhyItMatters: Undetected collisions make enterprise roll-up compare competencies that are not the same thing, which is exactly the CMM Level 5 failure mode.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-02.3.02 collision count, TLA-90.2.02); Assumption A-027
FollowUps: Is a collision count produced at import? / What is the disposition process per collision? / Who accepts an unresolved collision?
SampleAnswerShape: names the import-time collision report, the disposition record and the accepting authority

Question: When a crosswalk is invalidated by a new framework version, what happens to gap-training plans that were computed while it was valid?
WhyItMatters: Learners are already enrolled against a plan derived from a mapping the registry has now withdrawn, and nobody recomputes it.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-91.1.04); Architecture Review Report §D-M36 dependency
FollowUps: Are downstream plans recomputed or flagged? / Is the learner told mid-course? / Who owns the recomputation SLA?
SampleAnswerShape: names the downstream recomputation trigger, its SLA and the learner-facing disclosure

Question: When a supervisor screen shows a competency, should it display the identifier, the localised label, the framework version, or all three?
WhyItMatters: A screen showing only a label lets two different competencies from two frameworks look identical to the person making a deployment decision.
FollowUps: Is framework attribution mandatory on every surface? / What is shown when no label exists in the user's locale? / Does the rendering rule apply to exports?
SampleAnswerShape: names the mandatory display fields and the fallback when a locale label is missing

Question: If the registry blocks new writes against a deprecated competency, what does the assessment interface show a learner who is halfway through that assessment?
WhyItMatters: Failing at submit after the learner completed the work destroys trust in the assessment far more than refusing to start it.
FollowUps: Is deprecation checked at start or at submit? / Is the in-flight attempt honoured? / What is the message text?
SampleAnswerShape: names the check point, the in-flight policy and the learner-facing wording

Question: What is an official competency record in EdVidura, and which module is named as the writer of it?
WhyItMatters: A designer who does not know where competence is asserted will build assessments whose results never reach the record a supervisor acts on.
AnswerSource: Product Plan v2 (M12); Architecture Review Report §H.5
BlocksWork: D08 official-record schema; D15 Competency Assessment Tool
FollowUps: Who approves the write? / What is stored alongside the result? / Can it be amended later?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the writing module, the store, and the named human approver recorded on the record

Question: Why can a lesson not be tagged with a free-text skill name in EdVidura?
WhyItMatters: Free-text skill tags make gap arithmetic produce confidently wrong training plans, which the architecture review flags as a P0.
BlocksWork: D08 competency schema freeze before D14/D23 build
FollowUps: Where do the controlled terms come from? / Who adds a new competency? / What is the versioning rule?
SampleAnswerShape: Explains the ontology dependency and names the registry as the controlled source

Question: What is the difference between a competency, a competency level and a credential in the registry object model?
WhyItMatters: An instructional designer who conflates these will attach evidence requirements to the wrong entity and the resulting official record cannot be interpreted.
FollowUps: Where do prerequisite relationships live? / Does a credential carry validity and renewal? / What issues a credential?
SampleAnswerShape: defines all three entities and states which one an official record asserts against

Question: How do I add a new competency to the registry without invalidating assessments already mapped to the previous framework version?
WhyItMatters: An unversioned framework change silently re-points historical records to definitions that did not exist when they were earned.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §H.5; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-19.x)
FollowUps: Do records pin a framework version? / What is the deprecation path? / Who approves a version bump?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes version pinning on the record and the migration rule for consumers

Question: When a competency is retired in the registry, what happens to official records that cite it?
WhyItMatters: Retiring a definition out from under a live record makes every certificate citing it unexplainable to an assessor.
FollowUps: Is retirement a supersession or a delete? / Does it propagate to enclaves? / Who is notified?
SampleAnswerShape: States that records pin the version in force and describes the supersession record

Question: If a retired competency is still cited by a live official record, which version does a supervisor dashboard display?
WhyItMatters: Showing the current definition against a historical record misrepresents what the learner actually demonstrated.
FollowUps: Does the dashboard show the version? / Is there a as-at view? / Who chose the default?
SampleAnswerShape: States which version is authoritative for display and why

Question: What happens when an assessment tries to write a new record against a competency that has been deprecated?
WhyItMatters: If deprecated competencies still accept writes, the registry's lifecycle states are decoration and the corpus of records fragments across retired definitions.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-32.2.05 deprecation behaviour test)
FollowUps: Are historical records still readable? / What is the learner told mid-assessment? / Is there a grace window?
SampleAnswerShape: states that new writes are blocked, historical reads preserved, and names the learner-facing behaviour

Question: What is the blast radius when the competency registry publishes a bad framework version in the middle of a cohort?
WhyItMatters: Every downstream gap computation, adaptive path and official record made against the bad version has to be identified and reworked.
FollowUps: Can a version be withdrawn? / Who is downstream? / What is the notification path to enclaves?
SampleAnswerShape: Enumerates the consumers and states the withdrawal and re-computation path

Question: When an official record is revoked, how do you find every learner whose training path was changed because of it?
WhyItMatters: Unwinding a revoked record without finding its downstream effects leaves learners on paths built from a fact that is no longer true.
BlocksWork: D14 rule and signal versioning for traceability
FollowUps: Are path changes logged with their causes? / Is the cause queryable? / What is the notification path?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes cause-logging on path changes and a reverse lookup

Question: A catalogue entry references competency v1 and the registry publishes v2 that splits it into two competencies — which catalogue entry is now authoritative for each half?
WhyItMatters: Two products applying different resolution rules to the same split means a learner is offered training for a competency they already hold, or none for one they lack.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.2.03 crosswalk mapping format, TLA-07.1.01)
FollowUps: Does the catalogue re-link automatically? / Who re-tags the entry? / What does search return in the interim?
SampleAnswerShape: names the split resolution rule, the catalogue re-linking owner and the interim search behaviour

Question: Which is more expensive to reverse in eighteen months: a loose competency ontology or a loose evidence ladder?
WhyItMatters: Choosing the wrong one to firm up first means the expensive rework lands after content and records already depend on it.
FollowUps: How many records would need re-derivation? / How much content would be re-tagged? / Which blocks the other?
SampleAnswerShape: Compares rework volume and dependency direction rather than asserting a preference

Question: What should happen to historical official records asserted against a competency that is later retired entirely?
WhyItMatters: Retiring a competency without a rule either invalidates real certifications or leaves records asserting something the organisation no longer recognises.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.2.02, TLA-01.2.03); Architecture Review Report §D-M19 gap 3
FollowUps: Does the record stay valid or become historical-only? / Is the learner told? / Can the record still be presented to an employer?
SampleAnswerShape: names the record's post-retirement status, the learner communication and the presentation rule

Question: Which EdVidura products cannot start build until the Competency-Registry schema is frozen, and where is that recorded?
WhyItMatters: Scheduling competency-dependent products before the registry exists produces official records asserted against an informal vocabulary that may be unmigratable.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §D-M19 risk P0; Risk R-001; Master Checklist v3 (MOD-003)
FollowUps: Which of them are already in build? / What is the schema-freeze date? / What is the fallback if the freeze slips?
SampleAnswerShape: names the dependent products, the freeze artefact and the recorded critical-path risk

Question: The registry does not exist while two competency-dependent products are already scheduled for build — what sequencing is actually defensible?
WhyItMatters: Building the dependants first guarantees a mass record migration later, but holding them idle costs schedule the programme has already committed.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §D-M19 risk P0; Risk R-001; Master Checklist v3 (MOD-003)
FollowUps: Can dependants build against a stubbed contract? / What is the migration cost if we proceed? / Who accepts that risk in writing?
SampleAnswerShape: names a sequencing option, its cost, and the person who signs the residual risk

Question: What do we tell a customer whose competency framework cannot be expressed without extending the registry ontology?
WhyItMatters: Promising to model any framework commits engineering to unbounded ontology change; refusing loses the customer whose framework is their whole business.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-90.1.02, TLA-90.2.01 change-request route)
FollowUps: Is there a change-request route with an SLA? / Who pays for an extension? / What is the interim representation?
SampleAnswerShape: names the extension request path, its owner, and the honest interim modelling

Question: Where do I get a real competency framework to test the registry against rather than a toy fixture?
WhyItMatters: Tests that only ever load a handmade framework never encounter the vocabulary collisions and structural depth that break the real import.
FollowUps: Do we hold written usage rights for it? / Which two frameworks are committed? / Where are the fixtures stored?
SampleAnswerShape: names the fixture source, the rights record and where the versioned fixture lives

Question: What does an authorisation negative test look like for the supervisor role against the competency registry?
WhyItMatters: A supervisor who can write an official record they should only read produces unauditable competence claims.
FollowUps: What is the full out-of-role action list? / Is it derived from a matrix? / Who maintains it?
SampleAnswerShape: Enumerates every out-of-role action for the role and asserts denial

Question: What test proves a historical official record still resolves to its original definition after a framework upgrade, and what does that test not cover?
WhyItMatters: A passing upgrade test that only exercises unchanged competencies gives false confidence about the split, merge and rename cases that actually break.
FollowUps: Does it cover split and merge? / Does it cover a retired competency? / Does it run in the enclave build?
SampleAnswerShape: names the covered transformations, the uncovered ones and where they are accepted as risk

Question: How do the five registry consumer modules obtain a resolution client, and what breaks if each writes its own?
WhyItMatters: Five independently written clients produce five different caching, versioning and error behaviours, and the registry contract is effectively unenforced.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.3.04 client resolution decision, TST-32.2.04)
FollowUps: Is the decision recorded? / Does the consumer conformance suite exist? / Who maintains a shared library?
SampleAnswerShape: names the decision, the owner, and the conformance suite that holds consumers to the contract

Question: What does the third-party framework-load test prove about the registry, and what does it deliberately not prove?
WhyItMatters: Passing a MOSA load test with informal help from the module team proves nothing about recompetition, which is the point of the test.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-01.3.03, TST-32.2.02); Architecture Review Report §O.1
FollowUps: Was any assistance given? / Was the documentation the only input? / Does it cover crosswalk authoring too?
SampleAnswerShape: states the zero-assistance condition, the artefacts used, and the scope the test excludes

Question: What prevents a non-governance role from authoring or approving a competency framework?
WhyItMatters: Whoever can approve a framework can redefine what an official record means, retroactively, for every learner asserted against it.
FollowUps: Is approval separate from authoring? / Is the change history hash-chained? / What does an anonymous scan return?
SampleAnswerShape: names the authoring and approving roles, their separation, and the audit trail that proves it

Question: Should competency framework definitions be tenant-scoped or globally visible, and what does each choice cost?
WhyItMatters: Global frameworks leak which competencies an organisation cares about; tenant-scoped frameworks make cross-organisation crosswalks and CMM Level 5 far harder.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-03.1.02 framework visibility scoping); Decision Register DEC-006
FollowUps: Is a national framework a special case? / How does an enclave hold a global framework? / Who decides visibility per framework?
SampleAnswerShape: distinguishes public national frameworks from organisation-private ones and names the per-framework visibility decision

Question: What is the first diagnostic when a supervisor reports that a competency now shows a different label than it did last month?
WhyItMatters: A label change looks like a defect and is usually a framework version publish; without a first diagnostic every one becomes an incident.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-03.1.03 change-history audit trail)
FollowUps: Is the change in the framework audit trail? / Which version is the screen resolving? / Was a locale label edited?
SampleAnswerShape: names the audit-trail query, the version the surface resolved and the label-edit path

Question: Which two published contracts are exercised in the Level 3 demonstration?
WhyItMatters: A developer who does not know which contracts are on the demonstration path will harden the wrong service in the weeks before a dated event.
FollowUps: Are both contracts published and versioned? / Do both have conformance suites? / Which one is weaker today?
SampleAnswerShape: names the catalogue and profile contracts and their conformance status

Question: Walk the Level 3 demonstration end to end: catalogue query and profile exchange with an external system.
WhyItMatters: Without a walked-through path the first rehearsal discovers a missing authentication step on the day of a witnessed event.
FollowUps: How does the external system authenticate? / Which network path is used? / What is the rollback if a step fails mid-demo?
SampleAnswerShape: names each call, the authentication used and the abort behaviour

Question: What happens if the external partner implements the profile contract at an older published version?
WhyItMatters: Version negotiation improvised on the day either produces a false pass or a public failure in front of a witness.
FollowUps: Is the contract backward compatible? / Is a version handshake defined? / Does an older version still count as Level 3?
SampleAnswerShape: names the compatibility rule, the negotiation step and the evidence implication

Question: What is the rollback path if the demonstration exposes a defect that requires a change to a published TLA contract?
WhyItMatters: Changing a published contract after external parties have implemented it breaks the MOSA promise the contract exists to make.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-10.2.02, TLA-01.3.01); Architecture Review Report §S item 1
FollowUps: Is it a patch or a new version? / Who must be notified? / Does the demonstration have to be repeated?
SampleAnswerShape: names the versioning rule, the notification duty and the re-demonstration trigger

Question: If only one TLA contract can be hardened to demonstration quality this quarter, should it be the catalogue contract or the profile contract?
WhyItMatters: The profile contract carries privacy exposure and the catalogue contract carries content dependency; hardening the wrong one wastes the quarter.
FollowUps: Which is closer to complete? / Which is more valuable to the client? / Which is riskier to expose externally?
SampleAnswerShape: compares readiness, client value and exposure, and names the deciding criterion

Question: What learner data leaves EdVidura during the demonstration and under whose authority?
WhyItMatters: A demonstration that exports real learner data without a written basis creates a privacy incident out of a marketing event.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-10.2.01 profile federation decision); Risk R-025
FollowUps: Is synthetic data acceptable evidence? / Who signs the data-sharing basis? / Is consent needed?
SampleAnswerShape: names the dataset used, its legal basis and who approved it

Question: If the Level 3 demonstration runs in a connected environment while the committed deployment class is air-gapped, what does the demonstration evidence about enclaves?
WhyItMatters: A maturity claim earned in the easy environment is used to sell the hard one, and the enclave gap surfaces at customer acceptance.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §Q.1; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-12.4.02 enclave install)
FollowUps: Can an enclave participate in a live exchange at all? / Is a media-mediated exchange still interoperability? / Does the client know which environment was used?
SampleAnswerShape: states what the connected demonstration transfers to the enclave case and what it does not

Question: What does profile interoperability actually mean for a learner in the Level 3 demonstration?
WhyItMatters: If the demonstration exchanges an empty profile shell, the level is claimed on a transfer that carries no learning meaning.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-33.2.03); Architecture Review Report §D-M20 acceptance
FollowUps: Which profile fields cross? / Does history cross or only pointers? / Can the receiving system act on it?
SampleAnswerShape: names the exchanged fields and what the receiving system can do with them

Question: If the named partner uses a different competency framework, does a successful profile exchange still evidence Level 3?
WhyItMatters: Exchanging a profile whose competency references the receiver cannot resolve is a syntactic success and a semantic failure.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §P.3; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-91.1.01 crosswalk)
FollowUps: Is a crosswalk required for the demonstration? / What does the receiver display for an unresolvable competency? / Does that count as re-entry?
SampleAnswerShape: states whether semantic resolution is in scope and what the receiver does with unknown competency IDs

Question: What does TLA CMM Level 3 mean on this programme and what evidence does a level claim require?
WhyItMatters: A level claimed without evidence becomes an acceptance dispute at the integration stage, when it is far too late to arrange a demonstration.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §P.3; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-13.1.02)
FollowUps: Who scores the level? / Who accepts the score? / What is the current honest level?
SampleAnswerShape: names the level definition, the required demonstration and the accepting party

Question: What blocks the Level 3 demonstration from being scheduled today?
WhyItMatters: Every week the partner stays unnamed pushes a dated, witnessed event closer to the acceptance deadline with no slack.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-15.1.01); Architecture Review Report §P.4 action P-R5
FollowUps: Who is accountable for naming the partner? / What is the lead time for a partner agreement? / What is the fallback partner?
SampleAnswerShape: names the unmet precondition, its owner and the lead time it consumes

Question: What is the recovery path if the named external partner withdraws two weeks before the dated demonstration?
WhyItMatters: A contract deliverable with one partner and no alternate is a single point of failure on the acceptance path.
FollowUps: Is a second partner in reserve? / Can the date slip without breaching acceptance? / Who informs the client?
SampleAnswerShape: names the alternate, the schedule impact and the client communication

Question: What would have to be true for the programme to claim Level 3 without a dated third-party-witnessed demonstration?
WhyItMatters: If the answer is nothing, then the demonstration is on the critical path and must be resourced now rather than at acceptance.
FollowUps: Is there any alternative evidence form? / Who would accept it? / What is the reputational cost of an unwitnessed claim?
SampleAnswerShape: states whether an alternative evidence form exists and who would have to accept it

Question: Why does the programme claim Level 2, then Level 3, then Level 5 without Level 4?
WhyItMatters: A skipped level with no written rationale invites a client to challenge the whole maturity claim during acceptance.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §D-M21; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-13.1.02 L4 skip rationale)
FollowUps: Whose level model is being used? / Is the rationale in writing? / Does the client agree with it?
SampleAnswerShape: names the source level model and the recorded skip rationale

Question: Is a second EdVidura tenant operated by a different team an acceptable Level 3 partner, or does that hollow out the claim?
WhyItMatters: It is the only partner the programme can guarantee, and it is also the partner most likely to be challenged by a client.
FollowUps: Would the client accept it in writing? / Does it still test documentation-only implementation? / What does it not evidence?
SampleAnswerShape: argues both, names what the client must accept in writing, and states the residual weakness

Question: Who witnesses a CMM Level 3 interoperability demonstration and what artefact do they sign?
WhyItMatters: An undated, unwitnessed demonstration is indistinguishable from an internal test and will not survive an acceptance review.
FollowUps: Must the witness be independent of both sides? / Where is the record archived? / Is a video sufficient?
SampleAnswerShape: names the witness role, the signed artefact and the archive location

Question: What is recorded as evidence when the demonstration partially succeeds?
WhyItMatters: A partial success recorded as a pass makes every downstream maturity claim indefensible; recorded as a fail it may understate real progress.
FollowUps: Is there a partial-pass category? / Who decides? / What must be re-demonstrated?
SampleAnswerShape: names the outcome categories, the decider and the re-demonstration scope

Question: How would you detect that the demonstration passed only because both sides were built from shared assumptions?
WhyItMatters: A demonstration between two teams who talked daily proves collaboration, not interoperability, and the maturity claim rests on it.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §P.4 action P-R5 (recompetition test)
FollowUps: Did the partner build from documentation alone? / Were any clarifications given? / Is the clarification log kept?
SampleAnswerShape: names the documentation-only condition and the log that proves it

Question: Where is the Level 3 demonstration script kept and who may change it?
WhyItMatters: A demonstration script edited on the day to match what happens to work is not evidence of interoperability.
FollowUps: Is the script version-controlled? / Is it agreed with the partner in advance? / Is deviation recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: names the script's home, its change control and the deviation-recording rule

Question: How is zero manual re-entry proven during the demonstration rather than merely asserted?
WhyItMatters: Manual re-entry is the exact thing Level 3 claims to eliminate, and it is trivially invisible to a witness watching a screen.
FollowUps: Are request logs captured on both sides? / Is keyboard input excluded? / Who verifies the logs?
SampleAnswerShape: names the artefacts captured on both sides and who checks them

Question: What does the Level 3 demonstration prove about the contracts, and what does it explicitly not prove?
WhyItMatters: A single successful exchange proves a happy path; the client will assume it proves the contract is implementable by anyone.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §P.3; Master Checklist v3 (TLA-15.1.03)
FollowUps: Does it prove third-party implementability? / Does it prove enclave behaviour? / Does it cover error paths?
SampleAnswerShape: separates what a single dated exchange evidences from what a conformance suite would evidence

Question: What trust relationship must exist with the external demonstration partner and how is it established?
WhyItMatters: Exposing a TLA contract to an external organisation without a trust model is an unreviewed inbound path into the platform.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TLA-15.1.01); Architecture Review Report §G.1
FollowUps: Is it mutual TLS or a federated token? / Is the path opened only for the event? / Who reviews it?
SampleAnswerShape: names the authentication mechanism, its lifetime and the reviewing authority

Question: What does exposing a TLA contract to an external organisation cost in accreditation terms?
WhyItMatters: An external interface added late reopens the security control mapping and can delay the authorisation the whole enclave programme depends on.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §W answer 26; Master Checklist v3 (FED-02.1.03 accreditor concurrence)
FollowUps: Does the accreditor need to approve the demonstration path? / Is the path removed afterwards? / Does it change the boundary diagram?
SampleAnswerShape: names the accreditation artefacts affected and whether the path persists after the event

Question: What can support see if the external partner reports a failed profile exchange a month after the demonstration?
WhyItMatters: An external-facing surface with no support visibility turns a partner integration issue into an unanswerable escalation.
FollowUps: Are external requests correlated end to end? / Is the partner's request ID captured? / Is PII excluded from those logs?
SampleAnswerShape: names the correlation identifier, the retained request metadata and the PII exclusion rule

Question: What does a run team actually install at an enclave site for D09 today?
WhyItMatters: Support cannot restore or patch what was never defined as an installable unit at the site.
FollowUps: Is there an install package? / Who wrote the runbook? / What is the version story?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the installable artefacts and the runbook, or states that neither exists

Question: How do you prove that no superseded chunk remains retrievable from a local model's index after a manifest is applied?
WhyItMatters: Retrieval filters that pass on hosted infrastructure can be bypassed by a different local index implementation, and the enclave is where the safety risk lives.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §D2 M26 (supersession compliance gap); Master Checklist v3 AIA-09.1.03
BlocksWork: AIA-09.1.03 tombstones honoured at query time
FollowUps: Is the filter in the retriever or the store? / What negative corpus proves it? / How is it re-proved after an embedding change?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes a negative-retrieval test with a known superseded corpus and a stated pass criterion

Question: Which named external system is the authoritative technical-order and manual repository that D10 connects to?
WhyItMatters: Every downstream freshness guarantee, blast-radius calculation and enclave update bundle is unplannable until this system is named.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §D2 M25 (gap 1); Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.01
BlocksWork: CNT-17.1.01 repository naming and access agreement
FollowUps: Who owns the access agreement? / Does it expose an API or only publish PDFs? / Is it reachable from an Indian data centre?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the system, its owner organisation and the integration route, or states plainly that none has been named

Question: Walk the path from a revision landing in the source repository to a superseded chunk becoming non-retrievable in the learner chatbot.
WhyItMatters: If any hop in that chain is asynchronous and unmonitored, a withdrawn maintenance procedure keeps being cited with confidence.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §F Scenario 4 required design change; Master Checklist v3 CNT-18.1.01 to CNT-18.1.04
FollowUps: What is the ordering guarantee between tombstone and re-index? / What if the tombstone applies but re-index fails? / Who is alerted?
SampleAnswerShape: Names each hop, the event that carries it and the point at which retrieval is actually blocked

Question: What is the blast radius if the source repository is unreachable for six months?
WhyItMatters: The plan has no prolonged-disconnection policy, so content whose currency cannot be verified keeps being taught as if it were current.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-18.1.09; Architecture Review §D2 M25 (gap 5)
FollowUps: At what age does content get auto-suppressed? / Who authorises continued use? / Does the learner see the age?
SampleAnswerShape: States the degradation ladder over time and the point at which content stops being served

Question: Why block retrieval with a tombstone list rather than simply rebuilding the index faster?
WhyItMatters: Choosing rebuild speed over query-time blocking leaves an unavoidable window in which withdrawn procedures are still served.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §F Scenario 4 required design change (b)
FollowUps: What does the tombstone list cost at query time? / How large can it grow? / When is it compacted?
SampleAnswerShape: Compares the two designs on window length, cost and failure behaviour and defends one

Question: What fields must a revision manifest carry for the lineage service to compute which artefacts are affected?
WhyItMatters: A manifest missing a revision identifier or effective date makes blast-radius computation impossible and the supersession chain silently incomplete.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.04 (manifest format); Architecture Review §F Scenario 4
FollowUps: Where is the manifest schema registered? / Who signs it? / How are partial manifests handled?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the identity, revision, effective-date and supersedes fields and names the registry the schema lives in

Question: How is the set of artefacts affected by one manual revision computed across eBooks, lessons, quiz items and chatbot chunks?
WhyItMatters: An under-computed blast radius leaves stale derivatives live while the team believes the revision has been fully applied.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-18.1.03; Architecture Review §D2 M25 (gap 3)
BlocksWork: CNT-18.1.03 blast-radius computation via lineage service
FollowUps: What happens for artefacts created before lineage existed? / Is the computation transitive? / How is it tested for completeness?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the lineage query, its inputs, and how artefacts with no lineage record are treated

Question: How would you detect that one enclave silently failed to apply a supersession manifest?
WhyItMatters: Silent per-site divergence is exactly the Scenario 4 route to a technician following an obsolete procedure on real equipment.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-18.1.06, CNT-20.1.01; Architecture Review §F Scenario 4 detection
FollowUps: What receipt does an enclave return, and over what channel? / What is the alert threshold? / Who watches it?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes a positive-acknowledgement mechanism rather than an absence-of-error assumption

Question: How does a revision reach a zero-egress enclave that cannot poll the source repository?
WhyItMatters: A 'live' connection into an air-gapped site is an oxymoron; if the degraded path is not designed, enclaves silently run on the corpus they were installed with.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.02, CNT-18.1.02; Architecture Review §D2 M25 (gap 2)
FollowUps: What is the media cadence? / Who carries the media? / What if a bundle is skipped?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the media-manifest path, the update window, and what the enclave does between windows

Question: What must a learner see in the reader while a document is superseded but its replacement has not yet been published?
WhyItMatters: A blank page or a silent removal mid-procedure is a worse outcome than a clearly labelled withdrawal, and the client will judge us on it.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.05, CNT-18.1.05 (learner-visible transition state)
BlocksWork: CNT-18.1.05 re-publish workflow with learner-visible transition
FollowUps: Is the old text hidden or shown with a banner? / Who writes that copy? / What language does it render in?
SampleAnswerShape: States the transition state, the wording owner, and what the learner can still do

Question: What is a Technical Order in the client's usage, and how does it differ from a training manual we author ourselves?
WhyItMatters: An instructional designer who treats a controlled TO like ordinary courseware will edit safety-governed text that must be reproduced verbatim.
AnswerSource: Client SME (technical-order manager persona, Architecture Review §D2 M25)
BlocksWork: D10 scope definition and D12 digitisation intake
FollowUps: Who may amend a TO? / Does a TO carry its own revision numbering? / Are TOs classified?
SampleAnswerShape: Distinguishes controlled source-of-authority documents from derived learning content and names who controls each

Question: When a procedure is withdrawn mid-lesson, is it pedagogically better to hide it or to show it labelled as withdrawn?
WhyItMatters: Hiding content silently teaches learners that the platform is unreliable; showing it wrongly risks the learner using it anyway.
AnswerSource: None — undocumented; owed to the Pedagogy Design Review Protocol (D04)
FollowUps: Does the answer differ for safety-critical steps? / Who owns the wording? / Does an assessment in progress abort?
SampleAnswerShape: Takes a position, states the pedagogical reasoning and names the gate that should ratify it

Question: Who is the accountable content authority required to set the supersession SLA in writing?
WhyItMatters: Until a person holds this, no number exists for how fast withdrawn procedures must stop being served, and nobody is accountable when one is.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.03; Architecture Review §W Q28
BlocksWork: CNT-17.1.03 supersession SLA and staleness maximum
FollowUps: Is that authority the client's or ours? / What happens if they decline to set a number? / Can we ship without one?
SampleAnswerShape: Names a role and an organisation, or records that the decision has no owner today

Question: Which D10 checklist items cannot be scheduled at all until the source repository is named?
WhyItMatters: Scheduling unstartable work makes the plan look healthy while the critical dependency stays unowned.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.01 dependency chain; Architecture Review §E dependency analysis
FollowUps: What is the earliest date the agreement could realistically be signed? / What can proceed on a stub repository? / Who chases it?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates items blocked by physics from items blocked by preference and names the chaser

Question: If no content authority is ever named, who ends up signing the supersession SLA by default?
WhyItMatters: Unowned safety numbers default to whoever is nearest the release, which is usually an engineer with no authority to accept the risk.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.03; Architecture Review §M decision register
FollowUps: Can delivery accept safety risk on the client's behalf? / Is there an interim number? / What is the escalation route?
SampleAnswerShape: Traces the default path of an unowned decision and names who should stop it

Question: Which D10 design decision would be most expensive to reverse once three enclaves are in production?
WhyItMatters: Reversing a propagation or lineage decision after enclaves hold production content means re-issuing media to every site.
FollowUps: Is the manifest format versioned? / Can old enclaves read new manifests? / What is the migration path?
SampleAnswerShape: Names one decision, quantifies the reversal cost and states the hedge available now

Question: What maximum tolerable content staleness can we commit to an enclave customer in writing, and on what evidence?
WhyItMatters: A number promised without an evidence basis becomes a contractual liability the delivery model cannot meet.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §W Q28; Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.03
FollowUps: Does it differ for safety-critical content? / What is the penalty for breach? / Who signs on the customer side?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes a number with a stated basis and names who accepts the residual risk

Question: How would you test that a tombstone blocks retrieval before the vector index has finished rebuilding?
WhyItMatters: If the test only checks post-reindex behaviour, the dangerous window between tombstone and rebuild is never exercised.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-18.1.04, TST-38.2.01; Architecture Review §F Scenario 4 validation test
FollowUps: How do you hold the index rebuild artificially? / What is the assertion at query time? / Does it cover every retrieval surface?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes an ordered test that pauses re-index and asserts query-time blocking with a named oracle

Question: What must the prolonged-disconnection drill assert about what the learner actually sees after a simulated six-month gap?
WhyItMatters: A drill that only checks internal flags proves nothing about whether a learner in the enclave was warned.
FollowUps: Is the warning blocking or advisory? / In which language? / Does it appear in the chatbot as well as the reader?
SampleAnswerShape: States a learner-visible pass criterion, not an internal state check

Question: What does the revision-propagation SLA test prove, and what does it deliberately not cover?
WhyItMatters: A green propagation test that never exercised language variants or offline media gives false assurance on the platform's highest-severity scenario.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 TST-38.2.01 to TST-38.2.04
FollowUps: Does it cover cross-language variants? / Does it cover artefacts with missing lineage? / Is it run per release or per site?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates what is asserted from what is assumed, and names the residual risk

Question: What proves to an enclave that a supersession manifest it received on removable media came from the content authority?
WhyItMatters: An unsigned or weakly verified manifest is a channel for suppressing current procedures or reinstating withdrawn ones inside an air-gapped site.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-17.1.04 (signed manifest); Architecture Review §G.6 media-transfer risks
FollowUps: Where do enclaves get the trust root? / How is a key rotated across sites? / What happens on signature failure?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the signing authority, the verification point and the failure behaviour

Question: Where does a live connection to an authoritative repository conflict with the zero-egress enclave rule, and what is the defensible compromise?
WhyItMatters: An accreditation reviewer will ask this directly, and an answer that assumes outbound connectivity fails the ATO.
BlocksWork: CNT-17.1.02 detection mechanism per deployment class
FollowUps: Is a one-way diode in scope? / Who accredits the media path? / What is the residual risk statement?
SampleAnswerShape: States the boundary, the compromise chosen and the residual risk owner

Question: Where does a support engineer look to find when a given site's manual corpus was last verified as current?
WhyItMatters: Without a content-as-of view, support cannot tell a caller whether the answer they were given was based on a withdrawn procedure.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-19.1.02, CNT-20.1.02 (fleet currency dashboard)
FollowUps: Does the enclave surface it locally? / How stale can that view itself be? / Is it per language?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the view or query and the field that carries the verified-as-of timestamp

Question: What is the first diagnostic when a site reports that the chatbot cited a procedure withdrawn last month?
WhyItMatters: Without a defined first step, support escalates a potential safety incident as a routine bug and the exposure window grows.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-21.1.02 (supersession operator runbook)
FollowUps: Is there a severity classification for stale-content reports? / Who must be told within an hour? / Can support force a tombstone?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the first check, the escalation trigger and who is notified

Question: How is the list of learners who consumed a superseded procedure during the exposure window produced?
WhyItMatters: If the exposure cohort cannot be identified, the only remedy is blanket re-training and every official record from that window is in doubt.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §F Scenario 4 recovery, Scenario 16 (e); Master Checklist v3 CNT-19.1.01
FollowUps: Do chat logs record chunk revision? / Do reading events carry source revision? / How long are they retained?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the fields that must be on the consumption event and the single query that returns the cohort

Question: How would you test that a superseded document is genuinely non-retrievable in every environment?
WhyItMatters: Testing only the connected environment leaves the enclave and the offline caches still answering from the withdrawn revision.
FollowUps: What is the measured time to non-retrievable? / Which caches are checked? / Who signs the result?
SampleAnswerShape: Covers connected, enclave and device caches with a measured time each

Question: What does supersession mean when a customer says the assistant quoted an out-of-date procedure?
WhyItMatters: Support that cannot name the mechanism cannot tell the customer whether the fix is minutes or a media shipment away.
FollowUps: What is a tombstone? / How long until every site has it? / Who sets it?
SampleAnswerShape: Explains that the old revision must become non-retrievable and names the mechanism

Question: What is a tombstone in the content index, and what does it do to retrieval?
WhyItMatters: A support engineer who cannot explain tombstones cannot answer the customer question that follows every stale-answer incident.
FollowUps: Who sets it? / Does it reach offline caches? / How is it verified?
SampleAnswerShape: Defines the marker and its effect on what can be retrieved

Question: What is the process for requesting an emergency purge of a document from the retrieval index?
WhyItMatters: A slow purge leaves an unsafe procedure answerable by the assistant while everyone believes it was withdrawn.
FollowUps: Who authorises it? / How is completion verified? / What about offline caches?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the authorisation, the execution path and the verification step

Question: What provenance metadata must an AI-drafted section carry when an author accepts it into a lesson?
WhyItMatters: Content that entered courseware from a model without a provenance record cannot be re-reviewed when that model is later found wrong.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §D2 M23 (suggestion-provenance gap); Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.03
FollowUps: Is the prompt stored? / Is the model version pinned? / Does provenance survive translation?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the provenance fields and the point at which they are written

Question: If AI-drafted content is always draft-only, what stops an author accepting a full lesson unchanged in one click?
WhyItMatters: The draft-only rule is meaningless if acceptance requires no engagement, and the pedagogy gate becomes the only defence.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review §D2 M23 business rule; D04 sampling rate
FollowUps: Is edit distance measured? / Does unedited AI content get sampled harder? / Is the author's acceptance recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes a detectable signal and links it to the review sampling policy

Question: What does the DCT publish to the Enterprise Course Catalogue, and what must be present for the publish call to be accepted?
WhyItMatters: An author who does not know the mandatory metadata list will build lessons that cannot be published and will blame the gate.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.02, TLA-07.2.01 (publish contract)
FollowUps: Where is the mandatory field list published? / How is it versioned? / What is the rejection payload?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the contract, the mandatory fields and where the schema is registered

Question: What exactly does the publish gate block on, and what is the author shown when it blocks?
WhyItMatters: A gate that warns instead of blocks converts every authored lesson into remediation debt discovered years later.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.03, CNT-02.2.01 to CNT-02.2.03; Architecture Review MOD-014
FollowUps: Is there an override role? / Is an override audited? / Can a gate be disabled by configuration?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the three block conditions and describes the author-facing rejection

Question: How does revising a published lesson avoid corrupting the state of learners already part-way through it?
WhyItMatters: In-flight learners moved onto a changed lesson lose progress or are assessed against content they never saw.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-02.1.04, TST-35.2.03; Architecture Review §D2 M22 (gap 3)
FollowUps: How long do old versions stay servable? / What happens at course rollover? / Who decides a forced migration?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes version pinning for in-flight learners and the retirement rule for old versions

Question: What is the rollback path for a published lesson found to contain a dangerous instruction?
WhyItMatters: Without a rehearsed rollback, the fastest available remedy is deleting content that learners are mid-way through.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-02.1.05, CNT-06.1.03; TST-35.2.03
FollowUps: How fast can it be done? / Does it reach offline mobile copies? / Who authorises it out of hours?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the rollback mechanism, its reach and its authorisation

Question: Why should the accessibility check be a publish-time block rather than a post-publish audit?
WhyItMatters: Post-publish auditing at digitisation volume creates remediation debt no reviewer pool can ever clear.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review MOD-014; Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.03
FollowUps: What does a false-positive block cost an author? / Which checks can be automated reliably? / Which must stay human?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues the trade-off in terms of remediation cost versus author friction with a concrete threshold

Question: What lineage fields are written when the DCT publishes a lesson derived from a digitised manual?
WhyItMatters: Without lineage on authored lessons, a source revision cannot flag the lesson stale and the supersession chain stops at the eBook.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-02.1.06, CNT-03.1.02; TLA-07.1.02
BlocksWork: CNT-03.1.02 content lineage on every published artefact
FollowUps: What if the author typed the content by hand? / Are partial derivations recorded? / Who audits lineage completeness?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the lineage fields and the rule for content with no traceable source

Question: How does a lesson authored inside an air-gapped enclave reconcile with the connected catalogue?
WhyItMatters: Two-way content federation is a different problem from the one-way pipeline currently scoped, and undesigned reconciliation means divergent catalogues.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.05, CNT-06.1.02; Architecture Review §D2 M22 (gap 6)
FollowUps: Do enclave-authored lessons ever leave the enclave? / Who adjudicates an ID collision? / Is local authoring even permitted?
SampleAnswerShape: States the posture, the reconciliation direction and the conflict rule, or records that no decision exists

Question: Where does the DCT authoring UI run, and does an author reach it inside the LMS or as a separate application?
WhyItMatters: A front-end developer who assumes an LMS iframe context will build authentication that does not work for an author on a standalone site.
AnswerSource: Product Plan v2 M22 scope; Master Checklist v3 CNT-02.1.01
FollowUps: Does the author use the same identity provider as learners? / Is there an enclave-local authoring URL? / What roles exist?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the deployment surface and the identity route for authors

Question: What is a lesson template in the DCT, and who is allowed to create or retire one?
WhyItMatters: Ungoverned templates spread structural and accessibility defects across every lesson authored from them.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.07, CNT-02.1.03 (template governance)
FollowUps: How is a template change applied to lessons already published? / Who approves a template? / Is there a template review gate?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the template artefact, its owner and the change-control route

Question: How does an author link a lesson objective to a competency in the registry rather than to free text?
WhyItMatters: Free-text objectives cannot be sequenced, cannot be reported against and cannot support a competency claim later.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.01, CNT-02.1.01; Architecture Review MOD-003
FollowUps: What if no competency exists for the objective? / Who creates the missing one? / How long does that take?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the tagging flow and the escape path when the registry lacks the concept

Question: How would you detect that authors are systematically tagging lessons to whichever competency passes the gate fastest?
WhyItMatters: Gate-driven tagging produces a catalogue that looks fully mapped while competency reporting becomes meaningless.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-05.1.01 (publish attempts versus blocks by reason)
FollowUps: Is tag distribution monitored? / Who samples tagging quality? / Does P2 review tags at all?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes a measurable signal and names who would act on it

Question: When the author who wrote a lesson leaves, what does the next author need in order to revise it safely?
WhyItMatters: Undocumented authorial intent means revisions drift from the original objective and the competency claim silently weakens.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-07.1.01 author guide; E13 knowledge continuity
FollowUps: Is design rationale stored with the lesson? / Is the P2 review record readable later? / Who owns orphaned lessons?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the artefacts that must survive the author and where they live

Question: Are translations linked derivatives of a master lesson or independent documents, and why does that choice bind the whole data model?
WhyItMatters: This decision cannot be retrofitted once content exists, and getting it wrong makes multilingual staleness undetectable.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 CNT-01.1.04; Architecture Review §D2 M22 (gap 5), §V.3
FollowUps: What if a translation legitimately diverges? / Can a variant become its own master? / Who approves divergence?
