Question: If evaluation numbers must come from the enclave rig, how do you test refusal behaviour before that rig exists?
WhyItMatters: Testing on hosted models produces numbers that will not survive the first enclave run, and the release gate is set on fiction.
FollowUps: Can recorded fixtures substitute? / What is provisional versus final? / When must the rig exist?
SampleAnswerShape: Distinguishes provisional fixture-based results from gate-quality enclave results

Question: What does the inference API conformance suite prove, and what does it leave untested?
WhyItMatters: A green contract suite against a stub says nothing about behaviour under saturation on real hardware.
FollowUps: Does it cover priority semantics? / Does it cover degraded modes?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates contract shape from runtime behaviour and names the tests for each

Question: How do you prove that the artificial-intelligence evaluation gate cannot be bypassed at release time?
WhyItMatters: A gate that can be skipped under pressure is not a gate, and an unevaluated model reaching an enclave is unrecoverable remotely.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-11.1.01); Architecture Review Report MOD-010
FollowUps: Is the gate in the pipeline or in a process? / Who can override? / Is the override logged?
SampleAnswerShape: Shows the gate as a pipeline control with a logged, narrow override

Question: What is the argument for making the enclave rig the source of the published performance and quality numbers?
WhyItMatters: Publishing hosted numbers and delivering enclave performance is the gap a customer discovers during acceptance.
FollowUps: What does the rig cost? / What if hosted numbers are better? / How is the delta reported?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues for the constrained environment as the binding number and prices it

Question: What is checked on a model artefact before it is admitted to an air-gapped enclave?
WhyItMatters: Model weights are an unsigned binary supply chain into an accredited environment.
FollowUps: How does the artefact physically arrive? / Who runs the boundary scan?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the signed bundle, the SBOM entry, the hash verification and the boundary scan

Question: How is it proven that no request reaches a model without tenant context?
WhyItMatters: A single anonymous inference path defeats every tenant control layered above it.
FollowUps: What does the probe kit cover? / How often is it run?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the scan, the negative probe suite, and the zero-tolerance pass condition

Question: If two enclaves run different approved model versions, does a security finding on one apply to the other?
WhyItMatters: Per-enclave pinning means a red-team finding is model-specific and may not transfer, so a fix can be assumed where none exists.
FollowUps: Is there a per-model finding register? / Who tracks version spread across sites?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the finding register keyed by model version and the site inventory

Question: How is model provenance verified from the weights hash recorded in the model registry?
WhyItMatters: A hash recorded but never checked at load time permits an unapproved model to serve grading traffic.
FollowUps: Is the hash checked at load? / Who approves a model per deployment class? / What happens on mismatch?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the verification point in the serving path and the failure behaviour

Question: What does a learner see when the inference service is saturated rather than down?
WhyItMatters: Support cannot distinguish slow from broken without knowing what honest queue messaging looks like.
FollowUps: Is ETA shown for grading too? / What is the queue-time target per class?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the queue position and ETA messaging and where it appears

Question: What telemetry can a site operator read locally when learners report slow answers?
WhyItMatters: Without local telemetry the operator's only diagnostic is rebooting the appliance and losing queued grading work.
BlocksWork: AIA-06.1.02 inference SLO and operator runbook
FollowUps: Which alert fires at 70 percent? / Is queue depth per class visible?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the metrics, the capacity alerts, and the runbook entry that uses them

Question: How do you distinguish a graphics-processor saturation incident from a genuine model quality regression?
WhyItMatters: Sending a capacity incident to the AI team as a quality bug wastes the window in which capacity could have been restored.
BlocksWork: E04 admission control and queue metrics
FollowUps: Is queue time observable? / Is there an admission-control priority class? / Are eval probes running?
SampleAnswerShape: Uses queue-time and probe-score signals to separate capacity from quality

Question: What must the local model swap walkthrough demonstrate for the served model to be genuinely replaceable?
WhyItMatters: A model that cannot be swapped makes every AI capability a single-vendor dependency inside an air-gapped site.
BlocksWork: Shared inference service contract and model registry
FollowUps: Do embeddings have to be regenerated? / Are prompts model-specific? / Who owns the eval set?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the serving contract, the embedding dependency and the evaluation re-run

Question: What does a recompetable module boundary mean in EdVidura, and what would a third party need in order to rebuild one module?
WhyItMatters: An engineer who does not know the recompetability test will publish an interface that only their own team can implement.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report SectionO; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.01)
FollowUps: What must be published? / Who checks it? / Which boundaries pass today?
SampleAnswerShape: States the test as a third party rebuilding from published documentation alone

Question: Which module interfaces currently exist only as prose, and what would be required to publish each as a versioned contract?
WhyItMatters: A prose interface cannot be conformance-tested, so every consumer builds against an implementation detail that will change.
FollowUps: Which are highest traffic? / Who owns each? / What is the publication effort?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the prose-only interfaces with the artefact needed to publish each

Question: What breaks in the learning-record-store swap walkthrough, and how is each break converted into a contract requirement?
WhyItMatters: Every break found in a rehearsed swap is a hidden dependency that would otherwise be discovered during a real recompetition.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.2.02); Architecture Review Report SectionO.2.2
FollowUps: Which breaks are schema-level? / Who owns the new requirement? / When is it retested?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists break classes and the contract requirement each becomes

Question: Should the contract registry be a runtime service or a versioned static artefact repository, and what does each choice cost?
WhyItMatters: Putting the contract registry in the runtime path makes it a platform-wide failure domain inside every enclave.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report MOD-005; SectionC.1 A-018
BlocksWork: Contract registry design and M4 split
FollowUps: What is the enclave footprint of each? / What does runtime lookup buy? / Who decides?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues one option with the enclave footprint and failure domain made explicit

Question: What does MOSA conformance mean in EdVidura terms and which module boundaries does it apply to?
WhyItMatters: A developer who does not know a boundary is in scope ships it without a published contract and fails the conformance audit.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.01); Architecture Review Report
FollowUps: What counts as a module boundary? / Which boundaries are prose-only today? / Where is the contract registry?
SampleAnswerShape: Defines the standard in this programme's terms and points at the registry that is the source of truth

Question: How do I publish a versioned contract for a new module boundary so the PRG-06.1.01 audit counts it?
WhyItMatters: An unpublished boundary contract makes the module unreplaceable and directly breaks the openness commitment.
FollowUps: What version scheme? / Who reviews the contract? / How are breaking changes signalled?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the registry submission, the review step and the versioning rule for breaking changes

Question: What does the data-rights register require me to record when I add a new embedding index?
WhyItMatters: Embeddings derived from client content with unrecorded rights can block recompetition and content reuse later.
FollowUps: Who owns derived embeddings? / What happens on model change? / Does the register cover test fixtures?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the register fields for an artifact class and who approves a rights claim

Question: How is the MOSA conformance matrix re-issued at each stage gate, and what does a per-module rating mean?
WhyItMatters: A matrix issued once and never refreshed hides regressions on boundaries that were conformant a stage ago.
FollowUps: What are the rating levels? / Who assigns them? / What blocks a gate?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the rating scale, the assigning role and the gate effect

Question: How would you detect that a proprietary interface has crept onto a module boundary between two stage gates?
WhyItMatters: Interface creep is invisible in code review and only surfaces when a swap is attempted, by which time it is expensive.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.2.05); Architecture Review Report SectionO.2
FollowUps: What automated check exists? / Who owns the boundary? / What is the remediation?
SampleAnswerShape: Names a contract-diff or dependency check run between gates

Question: What does the LRS swap walkthrough actually prove about our ability to replace the learning record store in production?
WhyItMatters: A walkthrough in a test rig that never touches production data can create false confidence in an exit strategy.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.2.02); E02 learning records spine
FollowUps: What breaks convert to contract requirements? / Is data migration in the walkthrough? / What is not covered?
SampleAnswerShape: States what the rig covers, what it does not and how each break became a contract requirement

Question: Which front-end assumptions would break if the host LMS were swapped from Moodle to Open edX?
WhyItMatters: Launch-context assumptions embedded in the front end make the LMS a hidden hard dependency that no contract records.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report SectionM DEC-012; SectionD1 M7
FollowUps: Which launch claims are relied on? / Is the grade return path LMS-specific? / What is certified today?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the LMS-specific assumptions and where each is encoded

Question: Which front-end integration points count as module boundaries requiring a published contract?
WhyItMatters: Front-end boundaries treated as internal escape the conformance audit and become undocumented coupling.
FollowUps: Does an LTI launch count? / Do embedded dashboards count? / Who arbitrates?
SampleAnswerShape: Gives the boundary test applied to UI integrations with two worked examples

Question: What is the data-rights register, and which artefact classes must it cover per module?
WhyItMatters: Without recorded data rights, a recompetition is blocked by ownership questions nobody asked when the artefact was created.
FollowUps: Who authors it? / Which classes are contested? / Where is it held?
SampleAnswerShape: Names code, schemas, content, models, embeddings, test suites and docs as the classes

Question: Which proprietary components require a delivered exit strategy before purchase or build is authorised?
WhyItMatters: Authorising a proprietary purchase without an exit strategy locks the programme into a vendor on its most differentiated capability.
BlocksWork: PRG-06.1.04 exit-strategy documents before purchase authorisation
FollowUps: What must an exit strategy contain? / Who authorises purchase? / Which components are affected?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the walkthrough engine, the AR application, the XR titles and the AI components

Question: What is the failure path when an open-source dependency changes licence mid-programme?
WhyItMatters: A licence change on a core dependency can make an already-deployed enclave non-compliant with no upgrade path.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.2.01); Architecture Review Report SectionO.2.5
BlocksWork: PRG-06.2.01 vendor lock-in and OSS sustainability review
FollowUps: Who watches licences? / What is the replacement lead time? / What do deployed sites do?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the watch mechanism, the replacement path and the deployed-site handling

Question: Which module boundary is most expensive to leave prose-only for another eighteen months, and why that one?
WhyItMatters: Publishing contracts costs effort that competes with features, so the sequence must be argued from consumer count and change cost.
FollowUps: How many consumers per boundary? / Which changes most often? / Who publishes first?
SampleAnswerShape: Ranks boundaries by consumer count and change rate and picks one

Question: Is a standing quarterly vendor-lock-in and open-source sustainability review a real control or a compliance ritual, and how would we tell the difference?
WhyItMatters: A review that has never changed a decision is consuming senior time and producing false assurance.
FollowUps: What decision has it changed? / What would make it binding? / Who chairs it?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes an outcome measure that distinguishes a control from a ritual

Question: What is our exposure if an external assessor asks to run the conformance suite during accreditation and none exists?
WhyItMatters: This is a scripted, predictable failure on the one item written specifically to be tested by an outsider.
FollowUps: Can a partial suite be offered? / What is the recovery time? / Does it fail the whole assessment?
SampleAnswerShape: States the assessor-facing consequence and the minimum credible partial answer

Question: What failure modes should a conformance programme have registered before its first stage gate?
WhyItMatters: E05's risk register is completely empty, which means no one has yet imagined the programme failing.
FollowUps: Who owns each risk? / What is the trigger and mitigation? / Which risk is already realised?
SampleAnswerShape: Names three or four concrete failure modes with owners and early indicators

Question: If MOSA conformance is still graded name-only at the next gate, which downstream product's acceptance is affected first?
WhyItMatters: Conformance failures surface as other products' acceptance blockers, so the exposure is not contained to E05.
AnswerSource: Coverage Cross-Check §B2 matrix; Product Plan v2
FollowUps: Which products cite MOSA in their criteria? / Can they accept conditionally? / What is the earliest impact date?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the dependent products in order of exposure with the date each is affected

Question: Why does a buyer care about MOSA conformance, and which buyer types raise it first?
WhyItMatters: A product manager who cannot answer the open-interface question loses public-sector deals at the technical evaluation stage.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report SectionO; Product Manager
FollowUps: Which tenders require it? / What evidence is asked for? / Who answers the question today?
SampleAnswerShape: Explains lock-in avoidance and recompetition in the buyer's own terms

Question: What may EdVidura claim about recompetability today, given that no module boundary currently passes the MOSA test?
WhyItMatters: An open-architecture claim that fails a technical evaluation costs more credibility than never making it.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report Section D1 caveat; SectionO.2
BlocksWork: Tender response content on open architecture
FollowUps: What is the honest wording? / What is the roadmap to conformance? / Who approves the claim?
SampleAnswerShape: Gives permitted wording tied to the published conformance matrix

Question: What happens when a tender requires open-interface evidence that EdVidura cannot currently produce?
WhyItMatters: Answering that question badly disqualifies the bid; answering it dishonestly creates a contractual commitment to conformance we do not have.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-92.2.03); Architecture Review Report SectionO
FollowUps: What partial evidence exists? / Can conformance be committed by a date? / Who approves the answer?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the partial evidence and the dated commitment that is defensible

Question: Which lock-in inside EdVidura's own stack would a buyer's procurement team identify first?
WhyItMatters: The lock-in EdVidura has not named is the one the buyer will name, and being second to it is a credibility loss.
FollowUps: Which components are proprietary candidates? / What is our answer? / Who maintains the register?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the top lock-in candidates and the prepared response

Question: Does MOSA conformance help or hurt EdVidura's own commercial position, and where should the line be drawn?
WhyItMatters: Full openness makes every module replaceable including EdVidura's; refusing openness disqualifies the company from the tenders it targets.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report SectionO; Product Manager
FollowUps: What is genuinely differentiating? / Which boundaries must be open? / Who decides the line?
SampleAnswerShape: Distinguishes interfaces that must be open from capability that may remain proprietary

Question: Which of the four RED-rated proprietary components is most expensive to exit, and does its exit strategy justify the purchase?
WhyItMatters: Authorising a purchase whose exit strategy is weaker than its lock-in is the decision MOSA exists to prevent.
FollowUps: What is each exit's cost and time? / Who authorises the purchase? / What triggers an exit?
SampleAnswerShape: Ranks the four by exit cost and states the trigger condition that would force an exit

Question: Where is the contract registry, and what artefact types are published in it?
WhyItMatters: A tester who cannot find the published contract will test against the implementation and certify the implementation as the specification.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report SectionS change 1; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.01)
FollowUps: Is it a service or a repository? / Who publishes? / Is versioning enforced?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the registry, its contents and the publication route

Question: What is a contract test on this programme, and how does it differ from an integration test?
WhyItMatters: Confusing the two produces suites that pass in staging and prove nothing about a third party's ability to implement the interface.
FollowUps: Which pairs are consumer-driven? / Where do the suites live? / Who runs them?
SampleAnswerShape: Distinguishes verification of a published contract from verification of a deployed pair

Question: What is a conformance suite in the open-architecture programme, and which interfaces currently have one?
WhyItMatters: Interfaces without a runnable suite cannot be recompeted, which is the whole point of the open-architecture commitment.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §O.2.1; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.01)
FollowUps: How many interfaces are prose only? / Who closes them? / Is the suite a deliverable?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the suite concept and identifies the prose-only interfaces

Question: Where is the contract registry, and what does a contract version mean in it?
WhyItMatters: Testing against an unversioned contract means a consumer breaks and nobody can say which change did it.
FollowUps: Who publishes to it? / What is the deprecation policy? / How is a breaking change flagged?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the registry and the versioning scheme applied to entries

Question: What is an evidence bundle, and what has to be inside one before a task can exit its gate?
WhyItMatters: A bundle assembled from whatever happened to be available is not evidence, and the exit gate becomes a rubber stamp the programme later cannot defend.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (Evidence column); QA Lead
FollowUps: Who assembles and who reviews the bundle? / Where are bundles stored? / What is rejected from one?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the artefact types in a bundle and names the reviewing role

Question: How does an engineer outside the module team run that module's conformance suite from published documentation alone?
WhyItMatters: If the suite only runs with team-internal knowledge, the MOSA claim is false regardless of how the suite performs.
FollowUps: What setup is documented? / What fixtures are needed? / Who observes the attempt?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the runnability check as an observed attempt by an outsider

Question: How do you write a conformance suite that an engineer outside the module team can run from published documentation alone?
WhyItMatters: A suite that only its authors can run is not a conformance suite and fails the open-architecture test outright.
FollowUps: What setup may it assume? / What fixtures ship with it? / Who validates runnability?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes self-contained fixtures, documented setup and an outsider dry run

Question: What does the third-party runnability check actually prove, and what does it fail to prove?
WhyItMatters: A suite that runs is not a suite that covers, and passing the runnability check can create false confidence in the boundary.
FollowUps: What is the coverage measure? / Who reviews coverage? / What compensates for the gap?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates runnability from coverage and names the compensating review

Question: Which module interfaces on this programme exist only as prose today, and what is the testing consequence?
WhyItMatters: Prose interfaces cannot be conformance tested, so every claim of replaceability for those modules is unevidenced.
FollowUps: Which are they? / Who owns closing them? / What is the interim test?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the prose-only interfaces and the suites that cannot exist without them

Question: Should conformance suites be a contractual deliverable to the customer, and what changes if they are?
WhyItMatters: Handing the customer the suites makes replaceability real and also hands them the tool to fail our own releases.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §O.3; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.03)
FollowUps: What data rights attach? / Who maintains them after handover? / What if they fail on our own build?
SampleAnswerShape: Weighs recompetition value against the loss of control over release evidence

Question: Where does the third-party-runnable conformance suite promised by PRG-06.1.02 currently live?
WhyItMatters: The item's acceptance criterion is that an outsider runs the suite from docs alone; if the suite does not exist the criterion is unmeetable.
AnswerSource: Coverage Cross-Check §C2 card 33; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.02)
FollowUps: Which team would own it? / Is any module's CI suite reusable? / What documentation must accompany it?
SampleAnswerShape: Either names the repository and owning team or states the asset does not exist and who must build it

Question: What must a module conformance suite contain to run green from published documentation alone with zero undocumented steps?
WhyItMatters: Suites that assume tribal setup knowledge pass internally and fail the moment an assessor runs them.
FollowUps: What counts as an undocumented step? / Who plays the outsider? / How often is the check repeated?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the suite's inputs, fixtures, credentials story and the rule for what may be assumed

Question: How would we detect that a conformance suite passes only because the person running it works on the module team?
WhyItMatters: Insider-only pass results are exactly the failure the runnability item exists to prevent, and they are invisible internally.
FollowUps: Who is a valid outsider? / Is a clean machine required? / Is the run recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: Defines the outsider criterion, the environment reset and the evidence the run leaves behind

Question: If the conformance suite is built as owned test items, who runs it at each stage gate and what does a red result block?
WhyItMatters: A suite with no gate consequence becomes a report nobody reads, which is how conformance decays between gates.
FollowUps: Does red block the gate or the module? / Who can waive? / How is the matrix rating derived?
SampleAnswerShape: Ties suite result to gate decision and states the waiver authority

Question: If E05's risks are registered late, what evidence shows they were genuinely identified rather than back-filled?
WhyItMatters: Back-filled registers are detectable by assessors and turn a remediation into an integrity finding.
FollowUps: Are entries dated and attributed? / Is there a review record? / Does any entry predate the finding?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the metadata and process evidence that distinguishes identification from back-filling

Question: How does the exception for prose-only module boundaries interact with the security review of those boundaries?
WhyItMatters: A boundary with no machine-readable contract cannot be threat-modelled or tested the same way, and the exception can hide that.
FollowUps: Which boundaries are prose-only? / Do they get compensating tests? / When must they be formalised?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the exception set and the compensating control applied to each

Question: How is the conformance suite delivered to and executed inside an enclave?
WhyItMatters: A conformance claim that can only be demonstrated on connected infrastructure does not cover the deployments that matter most.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-06.1.02); Architecture Review Report
FollowUps: Does the assessor come on site? / How do results leave? / What is signed?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes delivery, execution and result extraction with the integrity control on each

Question: What does a completely empty risk register on a conformance programme signal to an external assessor?
WhyItMatters: An empty register reads as a programme nobody has yet imagined failing, which undermines every other conformance claim.
FollowUps: What would a credible register contain? / Who populates it? / By when?
SampleAnswerShape: States the assessor's likely inference and the minimum credible register content

Question: What evidence would justify declaring a language supported at the artificial-intelligence interaction tier?
WhyItMatters: Declaring support on the basis that the model accepts the language ships a measurably worse tutor to those learners.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-93.3.02); Architecture Review Report §V.2
FollowUps: Which metrics and thresholds? / On which model and deployment class? / Who ratifies it?
SampleAnswerShape: Names per-language fixed datasets, thresholds and the deployment class they were measured on

Question: How do you add a user-facing string to a web client without breaking the externalisation audit?
WhyItMatters: One hardcoded string is enough to fail the audit and to leave a regional-language learner facing English at a critical moment.
FollowUps: What message format is mandated? / Is there a pseudo-localisation build? / What fails the pipeline?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the externalised catalogue, the message format and the pipeline check

Question: Where is the language tier matrix, and what does supported mean at the assessment tier as opposed to the interface tier?
WhyItMatters: Treating an interface-tier language as assessment-ready ships untranslated-validity items into official records.
FollowUps: Which languages are committed at assessment tier? / Who ratifies the matrix version? / What blocks a tier claim?
SampleAnswerShape: Points at the matrix, names its version, and distinguishes the five tiers

Question: How does a source manual revision reach the Hindi variant of a lesson, and what does a Hindi-reading learner see in the interval?
WhyItMatters: A learner trained on a stale translated procedure while the English variant was corrected is a safety and an official-record problem at once.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §V.3 (Scenario 16); Master Checklist v3 (PRG-07.3.03)
FollowUps: Who writes the banner text? / In which language does it render? / Is the interval measured?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the linked-derivative model and the learner-facing currency banner

Question: What happens when a learner passes the translated version of an item but would have failed the English master?
WhyItMatters: A translated item that is easier awards competence that was never demonstrated, and the record is indistinguishable from a valid one.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §V.3 (V-F5); Master Checklist v3 (PRG-07.3.02)
FollowUps: Is the language recorded on the record? / Are items re-validated per language? / Who compares pass rates?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the re-validation requirement and where the assessment language is stored

Question: When a source revision flags every language variant stale, what disposition is applied to official records issued from the stale variant in that window?
WhyItMatters: This is the hardest question in the supersession scenario and the one a customer will ask first after a safety incident.
FollowUps: Are affected learners identifiable? / Is re-assessment mandatory? / Who decides?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the audit trail that identifies affected learners and the disposition rule

Question: What test would prove that a Hindi assessment measures the same construct as its English master, and what would that test not cover?
WhyItMatters: Without construct evidence a language variant produces records that are not comparable, which breaks cross-language competency roll-ups.
FollowUps: What sample size? / Who are the bilingual raters? / What about code-mixed responses?
SampleAnswerShape: Names a psychometric equivalence method and states its blind spots

Question: What is the recovery path when an entire cohort has been assessed against a stale translated lesson?
WhyItMatters: Without a recovery path the choice is between voiding valid records and keeping invalid ones, and both damage the customer relationship.
FollowUps: Who identifies the cohort? / Is re-assessment funded? / What is told to the learners?
SampleAnswerShape: Names cohort identification, record disposition and learner communication

Question: What test would show that the learner-facing currency banner actually renders in the learner's own language?
WhyItMatters: A staleness warning shown only in English is invisible to exactly the learners whose content is stale.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §V.3 item 2; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-07.3.07)
FollowUps: Is the banner in the per-language E2E set? / Which languages are covered? / Who owns the wording?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the per-language end-to-end journey that covers the banner

Question: If translated items must be re-validated before feeding official records, what happens to a language that cannot recruit enough bilingual raters?
WhyItMatters: The honest outcome is that the language cannot be offered at assessment tier, which is a commercial decision nobody has made.
FollowUps: Who decides to drop a tier? / Is the customer told? / What is the fallback?
SampleAnswerShape: Connects rater availability to the tier the language may be claimed at

Question: Is a translated assessment a new instrument or a variant of the master, and what does each answer cost the programme?
WhyItMatters: The answer decides whether every language needs its own validation programme or inherits one, which is a multi-crore difference.
FollowUps: What does equivalence testing cost? / What does full validation cost? / Which do we promise?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues one position and prices the alternative

Question: If the enclave-hosted model is measurably weaker in Hindi, should the Hindi AI tutor ship at all?
WhyItMatters: Shipping a weaker tutor to exactly the learners who need vernacular support entrenches an inequity in the product itself.
FollowUps: What quality delta is acceptable? / What is the fallback experience? / How is it described to the buyer?
SampleAnswerShape: Ties the ship decision to a measured per-language threshold

Question: Should a language be priced as a one-off translation or as a standing per-language operating cost?
WhyItMatters: Pricing it as one-off guarantees the recurring review, re-validation and evaluation work is unfunded from year two.
FollowUps: What recurs annually? / What triggers re-validation? / Who owns the budget line?
SampleAnswerShape: Enumerates the recurring items and argues for the pricing shape

Question: If a language cannot meet the assessment tier, can content and interface still be offered in it without implying certification parity?
WhyItMatters: Offering partial language support without explicit wording is read by the buyer as full support, and the gap surfaces at acceptance.
FollowUps: What is the customer-facing wording? / Is it in the contract? / Who polices the claim?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates the tiers in customer-facing language and names who enforces it

Question: How would you detect that a regional script renders incorrectly inside a headset before a customer sees it?
WhyItMatters: Complex-script shaping failures in immersive runtimes are a known failure point and are invisible in any desktop test.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-07.2.02); Architecture Review Report §V.4 (V-D3)
FollowUps: Which devices are tested? / Which engine versions? / Who owns the font selection?
SampleAnswerShape: Requires on-device testing per engine and script rather than editor previews

Question: What does the automated accessibility scan miss that a manual pass in a regional language must catch?
WhyItMatters: Automated scans pass content that is unusable with a screen reader in Devanagari, and the sign-off is then false.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §J.4 accessibility plan; Master Checklist v3 (TST-07.1.04)
FollowUps: Is there a language-capable tester? / Which readers support the script? / Is text-to-speech quality assessed?
SampleAnswerShape: Names reading order, script shaping and speech quality as manual-only concerns

Question: How do you construct a per-language evaluation set that functions as a release gate rather than as a report?
WhyItMatters: An evaluation that reports but does not block lets a language be declared supported on numbers nobody acted on.
FollowUps: Who ratifies the threshold? / Where does the gate run? / What is the override path?
SampleAnswerShape: Ties a fixed versioned dataset to a ratified threshold enforced in the pipeline

Question: In which languages is EdVidura contracted to answer a support request?
WhyItMatters: Answering only in English to a customer whose contract promised a regional language is a service-level breach on the first ticket.
BlocksWork: E06 language tier matrix support tier
FollowUps: Is the support tier committed per tenant? / Who staffs it? / What is the fallback?
SampleAnswerShape: Reads the support tier off the language matrix for the tenant in question

Question: Which checklist items cannot currently be scheduled because the environment they need does not exist?
WhyItMatters: Scheduling work into a missing environment produces a plan that slips silently and is only discovered at the stage gate.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §J.2; Master Checklist v3 (TST-10.x)
BlocksWork: E07 environment dependency in the plan
FollowUps: Which environments are missing? / What is the lead time on each? / What is the interim substitute?
SampleAnswerShape: Maps unschedulable items to the specific missing environment and its lead time

Question: What interim evidence do we offer a client at pilot for a product that has zero test assets?
WhyItMatters: Arriving at pilot with no evidence and no substitute story converts a coverage gap into a credibility gap.
FollowUps: Is manual evidence acceptable? / Who witnesses it? / What is the commitment date for real tests?
SampleAnswerShape: Names an interim evidence form, its witness and the dated commitment that replaces it

Question: Which deliverable is most at risk of an acceptance dispute because its test evidence is subjective?
WhyItMatters: A deliverable accepted on subjective evidence is disputed at final acceptance when payment depends on it.
FollowUps: Which criteria lack a number? / Who agrees the number? / When must it be agreed by?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the deliverable and proposes a measurable substitute criterion

Question: Where does a failed test get recorded on this programme today?
WhyItMatters: Until a defect log exists a failed test survives only in a chat thread, and the release gate assembles around a hole nobody can name.
AnswerSource: Checklist Audit Report F-04 and FIX-04
BlocksWork: E07 defect log with fix-item linkage
FollowUps: Does the defect link back to a build item? / Who triages it? / What stops a Done item carrying an open defect?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the defect log sheet and the fix-item link back to the checklist

Question: What are the thirteen sections of the post-development test checklist, and where is that list held?
WhyItMatters: A tester who does not know the sections runs functional tests only, and the module ships with no accessibility or recovery evidence.
FollowUps: Which sections apply to a non-UI module? / Which are AI-only? / Who checks the set is complete?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the sections from functional through to user acceptance

Question: What is a TestCaseID, and which checklist column is meant to carry it?
WhyItMatters: Without a case identifier a test item claims coverage that cannot be traced to any executable script.
BlocksWork: E07 traceability from item to script
FollowUps: Are all 325 test items populated? / Who assigns the IDs? / What if the script does not exist?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the column and the rule that every test item carries one

Question: Which test teams exist on this programme, and which one owns accessibility?
WhyItMatters: Tickets routed to the wrong test team stall, and accessibility findings in particular have nowhere to land.
FollowUps: How many items does each team carry? / Is the split proportionate? / Who resolves contention?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the teams and identifies the accessibility team by its code

Question: What is a waiver on a test section, and who is permitted to sign one?
WhyItMatters: An unsigned informal waiver means a section was skipped with no record, and the release gate evidence bundle is false.
AnswerSource: Checklist Audit Report item 12; Master Checklist v3 (Waiver column)
BlocksWork: E07 waiver authority per test section
FollowUps: Is the authority named per section? / Is the waiver reviewed at stage exit? / Can accessibility be waived?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the waiver field, an approver and a date

Question: Which test environments exist today, and which are named in the strategy but not yet built?
WhyItMatters: Planning tests into an environment that does not exist is how a whole test class silently never runs.
FollowUps: Does the enclave rig exist? / Is there a device fleet? / Is there a federation harness?
SampleAnswerShape: Distinguishes existing environments from planned ones by name

Question: What is an exit-gate evidence bundle, and what does one contain?
WhyItMatters: A bundle assembled from memory at the end of a stage is not evidence, and the customer acceptance depends on it.
FollowUps: Who reviews it? / Where is it stored? / What links it to the item?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the artefacts and the reviewing role

Question: What does zero open P0 and P1 defects mean at the release gate, and where is that count read from?
WhyItMatters: A count read from nowhere means the gate criterion is answered with we believe so rather than with a number.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-13.1.03); Checklist Audit Report F-04
FollowUps: Which register holds the count? / Who verifies it? / What about deferred defects?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the defect register as the source of the count

Question: If the defect log does not exist yet, where have the failures found so far actually been recorded?
WhyItMatters: The honest answer determines whether historical test evidence can be trusted at all when acceptance arrives.
FollowUps: Can past failures be reconstructed? / Who holds them? / Does any Done item carry an open defect?
SampleAnswerShape: States honestly where failures live today and whether they are recoverable

Question: How do you test the empty-tenant first-run state of a module?
WhyItMatters: A module that errors with no data fails at exactly the moment a new customer sees it for the first time.
FollowUps: What guidance should render? / Does it differ per role? / Is it in the regression suite?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes provisioning an empty tenant and asserting guidance rather than errors

Question: What happens when a user acceptance defect is found after the module has already been signed off?
WhyItMatters: Without a defined path the sign-off stands, the defect is orphaned and the release gate evidence is wrong.
FollowUps: Is sign-off revoked? / Who decides? / Does it reopen the stage gate?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the revocation or conditional-acceptance rule and the deciding role

Question: How do you prove an alert actually fires rather than merely being configured?
WhyItMatters: A configured alert that never fires is discovered during the incident it was meant to prevent.
FollowUps: Who receives it? / Is the routing tested? / What is the drill cadence?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes an induced-failure drill that observes the alert reaching a human

Question: How would you detect that the regression suite is green because it has stopped asserting anything meaningful?
WhyItMatters: A quietly hollowed-out suite gives the strongest false assurance available to a release board.
FollowUps: Is mutation testing used? / Is assertion density tracked? / Who reviews suite changes?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes mutation or fault-injection evidence rather than pass rate

Question: Which of the thirteen checklist sections will be waived most often under schedule pressure, and who should hold that waiver authority?
WhyItMatters: Waiver authority placed inside the delivery line means the sections that protect the learner are the first to be skipped.
FollowUps: Should the customer hold any of it? / Is accessibility waivable at all? / Where is it reviewed?
SampleAnswerShape: Places authority outside the delivery line and names non-waivable sections

Question: Is the current test-team allocation defensible when accessibility carries a fraction of the items that functional testing does?
WhyItMatters: A lopsided estate guarantees that the under-resourced discipline becomes the one that slips at every gate.
FollowUps: Is the ratio risk-based? / What would rebalancing cost? / Who owns the decision?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues from risk exposure rather than from item counts alone

Question: When is automation the right proof and when is a game day the only honest evidence?
WhyItMatters: Automating what needs rehearsal produces green pipelines and operators who have never recovered anything.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §J.1 operational acceptance row
FollowUps: Which failures need humans? / What does a game day cost? / How often should it repeat?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates deterministic verification from human-recovery rehearsal

Question: Should the quality function hold block authority over a release, and what breaks if it does not?
WhyItMatters: Without block authority the quality sign-off is advisory and the gate is decided by whoever holds the schedule.
FollowUps: Who can override? / Is the override recorded? / Does the customer see it?
SampleAnswerShape: Takes a position and defines the override path and its record

Question: If waiver authority sits outside the delivery line, what stops the programme stalling on unresolvable waivers?
WhyItMatters: An authority with no throughput becomes a bottleneck that delivery routes around informally, which is worse than no authority.
FollowUps: What is the decision service level? / Is there an escalation? / Is a standing exception possible?
SampleAnswerShape: Pairs the authority with a decision service level and an escalation

Question: What should the EdVidura test strategy explicitly stop testing, and who signs that decision?
WhyItMatters: A strategy that never removes anything grows until the release gate is unaffordable, and the removals then happen silently under schedule pressure with nobody accountable.
FollowUps: What is the current cost of the full gate? / Which suites have never found a defect? / How is a removal reviewed later?
SampleAnswerShape: Names candidate removals with evidence and the role that owns the decision

Question: What is a product-specific delta test and how does it differ from the thirteen-section standard template?
WhyItMatters: A tester who only instantiates the template believes a product is covered when nothing product-specific has been tested.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-STD); Coverage Cross-Check §B1 D5
BlocksWork: Test coverage dimension across sixteen products
FollowUps: How many deltas are enough? / Who writes them? / What makes a delta specific?
SampleAnswerShape: Defines both, gives an example of each and states the coverage floor

Question: Of the sixteen products lacking delta tests, which absence is most likely to surface in front of the client first?
WhyItMatters: Prioritising test creation by client visibility rather than engineering convenience decides what the client sees fail.
AnswerSource: Coverage Cross-Check §I D5; Product Plan v2
FollowUps: Which are client-facing? / Which gate another product? / What is the build order?
SampleAnswerShape: Ranks the sixteen by client exposure with the reasoning for the top three

Question: Once a delta test exists, what makes it owned for coverage purposes — a team, a named lead, or a CI job?
WhyItMatters: Different definitions of owned mean the coverage number can be moved without changing anything real.
FollowUps: What does the coverage check actually count? / Can it be gamed? / Who verifies?
SampleAnswerShape: States the counted definition and the anti-gaming check on it

Question: What is consumer-driven contract testing, and which producer and consumer pairs on this programme use it?
WhyItMatters: Without consumer-driven tests a producer ships a compatible-looking change that breaks a consumer in another squad.
FollowUps: Who owns the consumer expectations? / Where do they run? / What blocks a merge?
SampleAnswerShape: Explains the direction of the expectation and names at least one real pair

Question: What is the thirteen-section post-development checklist, and at what point in a module's life is it filled in?
WhyItMatters: A checklist completed after the fact is a document, not a control, and the first release that skips it will be the one nobody can prove was tested.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (TST-0x); Architecture Review Report §J
FollowUps: Who fills it in and who reviews it? / What are the thirteen sections? / What happens when a section cannot be completed?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the sections at a high level, the owner, and the point in the lifecycle it is completed

Question: Where does the test data for a contract test come from, and may it ever contain real learner records?
WhyItMatters: Real learner data in a test fixture spreads personal data into every environment and every developer laptop that runs the suite.
FollowUps: Is there a synthetic data generator? / Who approves any use of production data? / How is test data refreshed?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the data source, its generation route and the rule about production records

Question: Once a waiver has been granted on a gate, who is responsible for the skipped test after the module is live?
WhyItMatters: A waiver with no owner becomes a permanent hole, and the untested behaviour is discovered by a customer rather than by the programme.
FollowUps: Is there a waiver register with due dates? / Who chases an overdue waiver? / Does a waiver block the next release?
SampleAnswerShape: Names an owner, a due date and the escalation when it passes

Question: How do you build a backward-compatibility check where a consumer written against version N minus one passes against version N?
WhyItMatters: Without it every contract change is a coordinated release, which the programme's squad structure cannot sustain.
FollowUps: Where are the old consumer tests kept? / How many versions back? / What breaks the build?
SampleAnswerShape: Retains prior consumer suites and runs them against the new producer

Question: Which missing test environment invalidates the largest number of release gates?
WhyItMatters: Prioritising the wrong environment leaves a whole class of gate criteria unevidenced through an entire stage.
FollowUps: How many criteria depend on each? / What does each cost? / What is the interim substitute?
SampleAnswerShape: Counts gate criteria per environment and ranks by dependency

Question: Where should the boundary sit between the defect log and the checklist status column?
WhyItMatters: Overlapping registers mean an item reads Done while its rework is outstanding, and the burn-down stops meaning anything.
FollowUps: What links them? / Which is authoritative? / What is the reporting view?
SampleAnswerShape: Defines the fix-item link and names which register answers which question

Question: Over eighteen months, which omission costs more: no defect log or no contract registry?
WhyItMatters: Both are missing today and the programme can only fix one first, so the ranking is an actual decision.
AnswerSource: Checklist Audit Report F-04; Architecture Review Report §O.2.1
FollowUps: What does each unblock? / What is the rework cost of each? / Which is on the critical path?
SampleAnswerShape: Compares downstream rework rather than asserting a preference

Question: If a customer holds the conformance suites, who arbitrates when their run disagrees with ours?
WhyItMatters: A disputed conformance result with no arbitration rule stalls acceptance while both sides believe their own run.
FollowUps: Is the suite version pinned? / Is the environment specified? / Who is the arbiter?
SampleAnswerShape: Pins suite version and environment and names an arbitration route

Question: How do I register a new delta test so it counts toward a product's test-coverage dimension?
WhyItMatters: Tests written but never registered leave the coverage number unchanged and the gap unclosed on paper.
AnswerSource: E07 test and release system; Master Checklist v3 TestCaseID
FollowUps: What identifier scheme? / Who assigns the test team? / Does it need a CI job to count?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes the registration route from written test to counted checklist item

Question: Should delta tests be owned by the building squad or by the QA Guild?
WhyItMatters: Squad-owned tests are cheaper and faster but grade their own homework; guild-owned tests are independent but always behind.
AnswerSource: Test Architect; Master Checklist v3 Squad/TestTeam
FollowUps: Which tests must be independent? / What is the guild's capacity? / How is the split recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues a split rule with the class of test that must stay independent

Question: How do you reproduce a customer issue when no production learner data may be used?
WhyItMatters: Reproducing with real data breaches the data-protection posture, and not reproducing at all means guessing at the fix.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §J.3; Master Checklist v3 (ANA-91.1.02)
FollowUps: Where is the synthetic generator? / Can a tenant shape be cloned safely? / Who approves an exception?
SampleAnswerShape: Uses synthetic fixtures shaped like the tenant rather than extracted data

Question: What is the per-tenant configuration baseline, and which fields does it version?
WhyItMatters: Without a versioned baseline nobody can say what a customer was configured with when the failure occurred.
FollowUps: Is deployment class in it? / Is the language tier in it? / Who approves a change?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists branding, language tier, retention profile, flags, class and endpoints as versioned fields

Question: How does identity resolution match a source learner to a platform identity, and what happens to an ambiguous match?
WhyItMatters: An unresolved ambiguity resolved automatically merges two people's training histories into one record.
FollowUps: What are the match keys? / What is the tie-break order? / Who works the manual queue?
SampleAnswerShape: Names match keys, tie-break order and the manual review queue

Question: Should migrated legacy records appear in analytics at all, given they cannot support official decisions?
WhyItMatters: Including them makes dashboards look complete and makes every readiness figure partly unevidenced.
FollowUps: Are they visually distinguished? / Are they excluded from roll-ups? / What does the customer expect?
SampleAnswerShape: Takes a position on inclusion with explicit visual and computational separation

Question: When a customer asks for their own branding on embedded dashboards, what does that actually cost in an open-source reporting tool?
WhyItMatters: White-labelling is a paid-tier feature in most reporting tools, so a sales promise made without checking becomes an unfunded engineering programme.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §L R-028; Product Manager
FollowUps: Is branding promised in any current proposal? / What is the workaround and what does it cost per tenant? / Who says no to the request?
SampleAnswerShape: States what the edition supports, the workaround, and its per-tenant cost

Question: How is a source field with no target equivalent dispositioned during an incumbent-system migration?
WhyItMatters: Silently dropped fields lose history the customer believes was migrated, and it is discovered years later at an audit.
FollowUps: Is the disposition recorded? / Who signs it? / Is the customer told?
SampleAnswerShape: Requires an explicit recorded disposition per unmapped field

Question: How are migrated completions marked so they cannot be treated as official records?
WhyItMatters: Legacy completions promoted to official status create competence claims with no evidence chain behind them at all.
BlocksWork: E08 evidence-level policy for migrated history
FollowUps: Is a legacy flag stored? / Does the grade path exclude it? / Does the dashboard distinguish it?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the legacy marker and the decisions it is excluded from

Question: What reconciliation would prove a migration is complete, and what variance blocks cutover?
WhyItMatters: Cutting over on an unreconciled migration means the customer discovers missing history after their incumbent system is gone.
FollowUps: What control totals per record class? / What is the threshold? / Who authorises an exception?
SampleAnswerShape: Names per-class counts and control totals with a blocking variance threshold

Question: What does tenant provisioning actually create, across identity, course site, records store, analytics and retrieval?
WhyItMatters: Provisioning that misses one subsystem produces a tenant that works until the first learner touches the missing part.
FollowUps: Is it scripted or manual? / Who owns the runbook? / How long does it take?
SampleAnswerShape: Enumerates the five subsystems and names the runbook owner

Question: What is the rehearsed rollback if a migration corrupts a live tenant, and how long does it take?
WhyItMatters: An unrehearsed rollback on a customer's first day leaves them with neither the incumbent system nor a working platform.
FollowUps: Is the recovery window measured? / What query set verifies it? / Who calls the rollback?
SampleAnswerShape: Names a rehearsed, timed restore verified by a defined query set

Question: How is a tenant provisioned at a site where the provisioning bundle must arrive on signed media?
WhyItMatters: A provisioning process that assumes a network leaves the disconnected customer unable to start at all.
FollowUps: How is entitlement issued offline? / How is local identity seeded? / How is evidence captured without a network?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes signed-media delivery, offline entitlement and local evidence capture

Question: Which onboarding steps should remain assisted-only, and what does self-service cost us if we get that line wrong?
WhyItMatters: Self-serving a step that touches official records or tenant isolation hands a customer the ability to break their own data.
FollowUps: Which steps are irreversible? / What support load does self-service create? / Who records the decision?
SampleAnswerShape: Draws the line by irreversibility and consequence rather than by effort

Question: If the first customer onboarding rehearsal exposes a step that takes days rather than hours, what gets renegotiated?
WhyItMatters: A rehearsal finding with no renegotiation route becomes an overrun on the first real customer instead.
FollowUps: Is the timed record kept? / Who owns the go-live date? / What is the customer-facing commitment?
SampleAnswerShape: Uses the timed rehearsal record to reset the committed onboarding window

Question: What must be confirmed with the customer before any source extract leaves their incumbent system?
WhyItMatters: Extracting learner data without a lawful basis is a data-protection breach committed by us on the customer's behalf.
FollowUps: Is the sub-processor list agreed? / What is the notice wording? / Who signs it?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the processing agreement, lawful basis and notice before extraction

Question: How is a tenant offboarded, and what evidence proves the deletion actually happened?
WhyItMatters: Offboarding without a deletion record leaves the programme unable to answer a former customer's data-protection request.
FollowUps: What is the export package format? / How are retention holds handled? / Who verifies revocation?
SampleAnswerShape: Names export, hold handling, credential revocation and the deletion evidence record

Question: Where is the tenant register, and what does it tell me about a site's connectivity before I pick up a ticket?
WhyItMatters: Without it a support engineer promises a remote fix to a site that has no route in, and the commitment is broken on the first call.
FollowUps: What fields does it hold? / Who is the named customer administrator? / How current is it?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the register, its owner and the connectivity and residency fields

Question: A customer administrator reports that a roster import created duplicate users: what is the diagnosis path?
WhyItMatters: Duplicate learners split a person's learning history across two identities and every competency roll-up for them is wrong.
FollowUps: Was the same file applied twice? / What is the match key? / Can identities be merged?
SampleAnswerShape: Checks import idempotency and identity match keys before touching records

Question: How do you check whether a tenant has drifted from its recorded configuration baseline?
WhyItMatters: Undetected drift means a customer is running a configuration nobody tested and the failure is unreproducible in staging.
FollowUps: Is the check automated? / Which fields are compared? / Who approves an intentional deviation?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the drift check and the field-level deviation report it produces

Question: If duplicate learners were created by an import, what happens to learning records already written against the wrong identity?
WhyItMatters: Merging identities without a record migration rule either loses history or double counts it in every roll-up.
BlocksWork: E08 identity resolution and merge rules
FollowUps: Is there a merge procedure? / Are official records affected? / Who approves a merge?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes record re-attribution and its effect on official records

Question: Where should the boundary sit between the customer's own administrators and EdVidura support?
WhyItMatters: A boundary drawn too narrowly floods the desk with routine work; drawn too wide it lets untrained hands touch official records.
FollowUps: What may an administrator change? / What is training-gated? / What is audited?
SampleAnswerShape: Draws the line by consequence of the action rather than by convenience

Question: How is an alert routed to the service desk given an owning tier and a documented first response?
WhyItMatters: Alerts that reach nobody or everybody both end with the same outcome, which is that nobody acts on them.
FollowUps: What happens to an unowned alert? / Who prunes the catalogue? / Is routing tested?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes catalogue ownership, routing and the removal rule for unowned alerts

Question: Should lab fleet device management be an EdVidura product or the customer's IT responsibility?
WhyItMatters: Devices nobody manages fall behind on firmware and certificates until an entire lab stops syncing, and the argument about whose job it was happens during the outage.
AnswerSource: Support & Service Management (E09); Architecture Review Report §D-M33
FollowUps: What can EdVidura see about a device it does not manage? / Does an enclave customer allow a management agent at all? / What is in the support contract today?
SampleAnswerShape: Assigns the responsibility and states what visibility the other party retains

Question: What must be true before a module can be handed over to the run team, and who signs the acceptance?
WhyItMatters: Handover without the criteria met transfers an unoperable module and the first incident becomes a customer-visible failure.
FollowUps: Is the checklist binary? / Who is the receiving owner? / Where is the acceptance recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the binary criteria and names both signing parties

Question: If restoration at a disconnected site depends on a customer-scheduled visit, what should the contract say about it?
WhyItMatters: A service commitment that depends on an uncommitted customer action is unenforceable in both directions.
FollowUps: Is access a customer obligation? / What is the relief clause? / How is attainment measured?
SampleAnswerShape: Makes site access a contractual obligation with a defined relief mechanism

Question: Must a defect seen only inside a customer enclave be reproduced in our own environment before a fix may ship?
WhyItMatters: Insisting on reproduction can leave a site broken for months; waiving it means shipping an unverified fix into the environment with the least observability.
FollowUps: What evidence can leave an enclave to support diagnosis? / Who authorises an unreproduced fix? / How is the fix verified on site?
SampleAnswerShape: Sets a reproduction standard with a named exception route and an on-site verification step

Question: What regression would go undetected during operational handover with no delta tests on E09?
WhyItMatters: Handover defects surface as production incidents after the run team has already taken responsibility.
FollowUps: What is the highest-risk handover path? / Who would notice? / What is the recovery?
SampleAnswerShape: Names a concrete regression, its detection route and who currently owns the consequence

Question: What is a deployment class on this programme, and how do I tell which one a ticket's tenant is in?
WhyItMatters: Answering an enclave ticket with a cloud runbook wastes the only response window a disconnected customer gets.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-94.1.06 tenant register); Architecture Review Report §Q.1
FollowUps: Where is the tenant register? / Who keeps it current? / What if the class is blank?
SampleAnswerShape: Names cloud, on-prem and enclave and the register that records which a tenant is

Question: What does air-gapped actually mean for a customer site, and what can support never do to one?
WhyItMatters: A support engineer who assumes remote access exists will design a fix path that cannot be executed and the outage extends.
FollowUps: Can logs leave the site? / Who is on site? / How does a fix get in?
SampleAnswerShape: States zero egress, no remote session, and media-only transfer

Question: How does a customer at a site with no external network actually raise a support ticket?
WhyItMatters: If the intake route is unknown, incidents at exactly the least-visible sites are reported late or not at all.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-96.2.01 offline intake route)
BlocksWork: E09 service-desk tooling per deployment class
FollowUps: Who transcribes it? / What is the clock start? / Is there a phone route?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the offline intake route and when the response clock starts

Question: What are the priority definitions on this programme, and who assigns the priority to a ticket?
WhyItMatters: Priority assigned by the wrong party turns a cohort-stopping outage into a routine ticket and the restoration target is missed.
FollowUps: Can a customer set priority? / Who can change it? / What is the worked example for training stopped?
SampleAnswerShape: Quotes the worked examples and names the assigning role

Question: What is a diagnostic bundle on this programme, and what is in one?
WhyItMatters: Collecting the wrong artefacts at a site you can only visit once means the next visit is the real fix attempt.
FollowUps: Does it contain learner data? / Who sanitises it? / What is the media handling rule?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the contents and names the sanitisation review before it leaves site

Question: Where is the register that names the primary and deputy owner of every operational runbook?
WhyItMatters: Runbooks with a single owner become myths the moment that person is on leave, and support improvises during an incident.
FollowUps: Which runbooks have only one owner? / When were they last reviewed? / Who audits the register?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the register and the no-single-owner rule

Question: Where do I find the response and restoration targets that apply to an enclave customer specifically?
WhyItMatters: Quoting the connected-tier target to a disconnected customer creates a commitment the programme cannot meet.
BlocksWork: E09 targets per priority per deployment class
FollowUps: Does the enclave column exist? / What does it say about remote access? / Who agreed it?
SampleAnswerShape: Points at the per-deployment-class target table and its enclave column

Question: What is a knowledge-base article's review date, and why does it matter to a support engineer?
WhyItMatters: Following a stale article at a customer site applies a procedure that no longer matches the shipped behaviour.
BlocksWork: E09 knowledge base seeding and ownership
FollowUps: Who owns each article? / What happens past the review date? / Is it visible to the customer?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the owner and review-date fields and the expiry behaviour

Question: What is the ready-for-operations checklist, and who signs it before support inherits a module?
WhyItMatters: Accepting a module without it means support owns a component with no runbook, no alerts and no rehearsed restore.
FollowUps: What are the binary criteria? / Who is the receiving run team? / Can it be waived?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists the binary criteria and names the receiving and signing roles

Question: What am I permitted to change in a production environment on my first week?
WhyItMatters: An unauthorised production change during an incident destroys the evidence and can breach the accreditation baseline.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-99.1.06 access tied to enablement)
FollowUps: What requires a change record? / Who approves an emergency change? / Is it different in an enclave?
SampleAnswerShape: States the default of no direct change and names the approved exception path

Question: If the offline ticket intake route is manual, when does the response clock actually start for an enclave customer?
WhyItMatters: A clock that starts at transcription rather than at the customer's report makes attainment figures look good while the customer waits.
FollowUps: Is the customer's timestamp recorded? / Who reconciles the two? / Is the gap reported?
SampleAnswerShape: States which timestamp starts the clock and how the gap is recorded

Question: If a runbook has only one owner, what is support supposed to do when that person is unavailable during a P1?
WhyItMatters: The honest answer is usually improvisation, and naming that is what gets the deputy appointed.
FollowUps: Which runbooks are bus factor one? / Is there a rota? / What is the interim procedure?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the bus-factor register and the interim escalation

Question: What are the steps to collect diagnostics from an air-gapped site when there is no network path in or out?
WhyItMatters: Getting the collection wrong means a second site visit, which for a disconnected customer can be weeks away.
FollowUps: Who performs the collection? / What is the sanitisation review? / Who authorises media removal?
SampleAnswerShape: Sequences on-site collection, sanitisation review and media handling

Question: How does a corrective fix actually reach an enclave site, and who physically carries it?
WhyItMatters: Assuming a normal release path for a disconnected customer means the fix is announced but never arrives.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §G.6; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-94.1.04)
FollowUps: Who signs the bundle? / What is the boundary scan? / What is the two-person rule?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes signed media, boundary scan and the on-site application step

Question: How is a support request written in a regional language routed and answered end to end?
WhyItMatters: A request nobody in the rota can read sits untriaged while the restoration clock runs.
FollowUps: Who translates? / Is the response in-language? / Is translation quality checked?
SampleAnswerShape: Traces intake, routing to a language-capable tier and in-language response

Question: What happens to a ticket for a module that has no named operational owner?
WhyItMatters: Ownerless modules mean tickets circulate until somebody adopts them, and the restoration target is already gone.
FollowUps: Is there an unowned-module list? / Who is the default owner? / Does it block release?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the ownership register and the default escalation for gaps

Question: How do you verify that an alert which just fired actually has an owning tier and a documented first response?
WhyItMatters: Alerts with no owner train the desk to ignore alerts, and the one that matters is ignored with the rest.
FollowUps: Where is the alert catalogue? / What is the unowned-alert policy? / Who prunes it?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the catalogue, the owning tier field and the removal rule

Question: What must a shift handover record contain so that nothing is lost between on-call rotations?
WhyItMatters: A thin handover means the incoming engineer restarts diagnosis and the customer repeats their story.
FollowUps: Is there a template? / Is it audited? / What about cross-language handover?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the template fields including open incidents and pending customer commitments

Question: If a fix must travel by signed media, what does support tell the customer about when their incident will be resolved?
WhyItMatters: Quoting a resolution time that depends on an unscheduled site visit creates a broken commitment on a P1.
FollowUps: Is a visit already scheduled? / Who pays for an expedited visit? / What is the interim workaround?
SampleAnswerShape: Ties the resolution estimate to the next scheduled access rather than to engineering time

Question: What can support actually observe when an air-gapped customer reports a failure, and what is inference?
WhyItMatters: Presenting inference as observation to a defence customer destroys credibility the first time the inference is wrong.
FollowUps: What telemetry exists on site? / Who reads it? / What can be exported?
SampleAnswerShape: Separates on-site observable telemetry from what support is guessing

Question: What is the honest restoration target for a site reachable only by a scheduled on-site visit?
WhyItMatters: An unachievable target agreed at contract time becomes a breach at the first incident and a commercial dispute after that.
FollowUps: What is the visit cadence? / Is emergency access possible? / Who signs the target?
SampleAnswerShape: Derives the target from access cadence rather than from engineering fix time

Question: Which of our operational runbooks have been walked end to end by someone who did not write them, and which have not?
WhyItMatters: An unwalked runbook is a document, not a procedure, and it fails in the one incident it was written for.
FollowUps: Is the walk evidenced? / Who witnessed it? / What is the re-walk cadence?
SampleAnswerShape: Names the walk evidence artefact and distinguishes walked from written

Question: What is the escalation when a fix must travel by media and the media is rejected at the customer's boundary?
WhyItMatters: Without an escalation the incident stalls indefinitely with support believing the fix was delivered.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §G.6; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-96.2.04)
BlocksWork: E09 escalation matrix for enclave delivery
FollowUps: Who owns the boundary relationship? / What is the alternative delivery? / Is there a customer escalation contact?
SampleAnswerShape: Names both the technical alternative and the customer-side escalation path

Question: How do you triage when the same alert fires simultaneously across every tenant?
WhyItMatters: Treating a shared-platform failure as many tenant incidents multiplies the response effort and delays the single real fix.
FollowUps: What is the major-incident threshold? / Who declares? / How are customers told at once?
SampleAnswerShape: Escalates to a single incident with one communication rather than per-tenant tickets

Question: What do you do during an incident when the only person who understands the failing subsystem is unreachable?
WhyItMatters: Waiting is a decision; making it silently is how a P1 runs for a shift with no progress and no escalation.
FollowUps: Is there a deputy? / What is the time-boxed escalation? / Is the gap logged as a risk?
SampleAnswerShape: Time-boxes the wait, escalates, and records the bus-factor exposure

Question: How do you run the customer communication cadence for a major incident when the customer cannot be reached electronically?
WhyItMatters: A disconnected customer discovers the incident from their own users, which is the worst possible first notification.
BlocksWork: E09 incident communication for enclave sites
FollowUps: Is there a phone or liaison route? / Who is the named contact? / What is the cadence?
SampleAnswerShape: Names an out-of-band contact route and a committed update cadence

Question: What evidence must be preserved before restarting a service during a suspected data-integrity incident?
WhyItMatters: A restart that clears the queue also clears the proof of what was lost, and the investigation cannot then conclude.
AnswerSource: Architecture Review Report §H.3; Master Checklist v3 (PRG-96.2.07)
FollowUps: What is captured first? / Who authorises the restart? / Where is the evidence stored?
SampleAnswerShape: Lists queue state, logs and counts captured before any restorative action

Question: If enclave telemetry cannot leave the site, how does the programme learn about failure patterns across enclave customers at all?
WhyItMatters: Without aggregated learning each enclave repeats the same failures and no product fix is ever prioritised.
FollowUps: What may be carried out as a sanitised summary? / Who reviews it? / Is it fed to engineering?
SampleAnswerShape: Describes a sanitised, human-carried feedback path with a review owner

Question: If a major incident is declared for a disconnected customer, when does the incident clock stop given restoration cannot be verified remotely?
WhyItMatters: An incident closed on assumption is reopened by the customer, and the attainment figures become meaningless.
FollowUps: Who confirms restoration? / Is customer confirmation required? / How is it recorded?
SampleAnswerShape: Requires an on-site or customer confirmation before closure

Question: What service level can EdVidura honestly offer a zero-egress site, and what should it refuse to offer?
WhyItMatters: Selling a target that depends on remote access to a customer who forbids it guarantees a breach in the first quarter.
FollowUps: What drives the number, access or engineering? / What is refused? / Who signs the refusal?
SampleAnswerShape: Grounds the offer in access cadence and names what is explicitly excluded

Question: Should support be permitted to change anything in production, or must every fix travel through a release?
WhyItMatters: Direct production change is fast and destroys the accreditation baseline; release-only is safe and can be too slow to save a training day.
AnswerSource: Master Checklist v3 (PRG-99.1.03); Architecture Review Report §G.7
FollowUps: What is the emergency change path? / Who approves it? / How is it evidenced for the accreditor?
SampleAnswerShape: Argues one position and defines the emergency exception with its evidence

Question: Is an on-site responder model or a customer-trained first line the right shape for Indian defence sites?
WhyItMatters: Choosing wrongly means either an unaffordable travel bill or a customer team blamed for outages they cannot fix.
FollowUps: Who trains the customer team? / What can they be authorised to do? / What does travel cost per incident?
SampleAnswerShape: Compares cost, speed and accountability of the two models

Question: Which support capability is currently at bus factor one, and what would you fix first?
WhyItMatters: The first serious incident in a single-person capability becomes an outage measured in days rather than hours.
FollowUps: What is the assessment method? / What does pairing cost? / Which capability is most consequential?
SampleAnswerShape: Ranks capabilities by consequence rather than by convenience of training

Question: Should support entitlement be sold per site or per seat for customers whose sites are disconnected?
WhyItMatters: The wrong unit means either the customer pays for capacity they cannot use or EdVidura absorbs unbounded visit costs.
FollowUps: How are on-site visits counted? / What is the overage rule? / How is it enforced technically?
SampleAnswerShape: Ties the commercial unit to the actual cost driver of disconnected support

Question: At what point does an operational workaround become an undocumented permanent feature, and how do you stop it?
WhyItMatters: Workarounds that outlive their incident become the real system, and the next engineer inherits behaviour nobody designed.
FollowUps: Are workarounds registered? / Do they have expiry? / Who reviews them?
SampleAnswerShape: Proposes a registered workaround with an expiry and a linked permanent fix

Question: What would have to be true before EdVidura could offer any remote diagnostic capability into an enclave?
WhyItMatters: Assuming this will eventually be granted shapes the whole support model around a capability the customer may never allow.
FollowUps: What would the accreditor require? / Is a one-way diode viable? / Who negotiates it?
SampleAnswerShape: States the accreditation and technical preconditions honestly

Question: Should the knowledge base be owned by support or by engineering, and what breaks under each choice?
